attendance.title: HR 3 — Attendance & Shifts
attendance.desc: The working rhythm: attendance captured not remembered, the capture machinery and its health reads, shift types from the trading calendar, the multi-branch roster with coverage and fairness, lateness and regularisation, the reads and the fair escalation path, and the monthly attendance close across the payroll boundary.

lessons.title: Chapter 1 — Attendance is captured, not remembered
lessons.html:
The people layer's daily heartbeat: who came to work, when, for how long. Module 3's thesis is the academy's oldest conviction at its most literal — attendance is captured, not remembered — because attendance is the people data with the shortest honest memory and the longest consequences.

Why attendance matters this much. Four reasons, each with its own reader: the payroll boundary — days worked and absences are the largest input HR hands across (Chapter 7), and the input's quality IS the salary's accuracy: the firm whose attendance is approximate pays approximately, in both directions, forever; fairness — the colleague who is always on time subsidises the one who is not IF nobody can see the difference: captured attendance makes punctuality visible, which protects the punctual (the academy's protections framing, at the door of the shop); capacity — for a trading firm the roster IS the branch's trading capacity (the till that opens late sells late; the branch that cannot cover Saturday loses Saturday — Chapter 4's terrain), so attendance is an operations number before it is an HR number; and evidence — the attendance record is load-bearing in every downstream process this track will build: the appraisal (module 5), the disciplinary process (module 7), the dispute where the tribunal asks what the records show, and the answer is either a system or a shrug.

The disease this module cures. The paper register — the exercise book at the counter where staff sign in, times self-reported and generous, pages that tear, a record that answers to whoever holds the pen — and its digital twin, the spreadsheet filled weekly from memory. Both share the fatal property: they are RECONSTRUCTIONS, written after the fact by interested parties, and every conviction this academy holds about reconstructions applies — the count made from memory, the cash-up done tomorrow, the project P&L assembled at job's end: negotiations, not records. Capture at the MOMENT, by a mechanism the person doesn't author, is the only attendance worth building policy on — Chapter 2's machinery.

The tone, set deliberately. One more framing before the machinery, because attendance systems are where implementations meet workforce resistance first: capture is not surveillance theatre, and the consultant who lets it be introduced as distrust has lost the room before the device is mounted. The honest introduction — the one that works — runs on the protections: the captured record protects YOUR punctuality from the register's politics, guarantees YOUR overtime is visible, makes the roster's fairness auditable, and ends the era of the supervisor's memory deciding who was late. A workforce that hears this makes the firm fair adopts in weeks; one that hears this catches you games the machinery from day one (Chapter 9's proxy pattern) — and the difference is entirely in the introduction, which is why this paragraph is curriculum and not garnish.

lessons.title: Chapter 2 — The capture machinery
lessons.html:
The moment of truth, mechanised: how presence becomes a record without passing through anyone's memory or generosity. The capture chapter.

The methods, matched to the workforce. The branch device — the biometric or badge terminal at the branch door: the trading firm's workhorse, because it captures at the physical threshold (present means present HERE), resists delegation (the fingerprint doesn't lend — Chapter 9's proxy fraud is the badge's disease and biometrics' argument), and works for staff who never touch a computer. Mobile check-in — the phone-based check-in with location capture: the field workforce's method (the delivery driver at the depot, the field salesperson at the territory — the van custodian of Inventory 6 checking in where the van is), governed by the location rules the role defines (checked in from WHERE matters when the where is the job). The system session — for desk staff whose login is their presence, the lightest capture. The design law across all three: the method fits the ROLE (the storekeeper badges at the branch; the driver checks in on the road; the accountant's session suffices), one person may have one method, and every method lands in the SAME attendance record — the capture diversity converging on one truth, exactly as the payment modes of Accounts 3 converged on one bank layer.

From check-in to attendance record. The machinery's flow: the check-in/out EVENTS (timestamped, sourced, located where relevant) accumulate raw; the system MARKS attendance from them against the person's shift (Chapter 3) — present, late (past grace), half-day (past the threshold), absent (no events against a rostered shift) — and the marked attendance record per person per day is the layer everything downstream reads. The separation matters and is worth teaching explicitly: EVENTS are facts (the badge fired at 8:47), MARKS are judgments applied by policy (8:47 against an 8:30 shift with 15 minutes' grace = late) — and policy changes (the grace widened) re-mark without rewriting facts, which is the GL-and-reports separation of Accounts 1, beating in the attendance layer.

Manual marking: the exception with a document. The capture will miss — the device down, the power out, the phone dead — and the system's answer is never the register's return: manual attendance is an EXCEPTION flow (marked by the authorised role, reasoned, visible as manual in every read — the manual mark that looks identical to a captured one poisons the record's authority), and sustained manual marking is a maintenance alarm, not a workaround culture (the branch whose device has been 'down' for a month has re-invented the exercise book with extra steps — the read Chapter 9 watches). The regularisation REQUEST — the employee-initiated correction for the forgot-to-badge morning — is Chapter 5's machinery: same principle, employee's side, approval riding the spine.

The capture health read. The layer's own vital signs, read weekly by HR in minutes: capture rate (events per rostered shift — the falling rate is devices failing or discipline fading), manual-mark share (the exception staying exceptional), and orphan events (check-ins with no check-out — the pattern that is sometimes forgetfulness and sometimes the early leaver's habit). A capture layer read this way stays trustworthy; one never read decays into the approximate record it replaced — the master-data law's daily edition.

lessons.title: Chapter 3 — Shift types & assignments
lessons.html:
Attendance judges presence AGAINST an expectation, and the expectation is the SHIFT — defined once, assigned deliberately, and honest about the trading week it serves. The expectation chapter.

The shift type: policy in a record. Each shift type defines its window (start, end), its GRACE (the minutes past start before late begins — a policy number, set deliberately and applied evenly: the grace that flexes per person is the register's politics returned), its thresholds (the late-arrival and early-exit lines; the point past which the day marks half), and its break conventions. The trading firm's working set is small and real: the OPENING shift (the till that must be counted in before the doors — Accounts 3's session discipline giving the shift its start), the CLOSING shift (cash-up inside the window — the closer's day ends when the session ties, and the shift says so), the STANDARD day for office and warehouse, the WEEKEND shifts the retail week demands, and the MARKET-DAY pattern where the trade has one (the early start that meets the supply run — Inventory 6's run calendar and this chapter describing the same morning from two sides). The design law: shifts are defined from the TRADING CALENDAR, not from office habit — the branch's shifts exist so the branch's hours are covered, which makes shift design an operations conversation the consultant hosts with the branch manager, not an HR default accepted silently.

Assignment: default and roster. Two assignment modes, used together: the DEFAULT shift (the standing pattern — the accountant's standard day, set once on the record and inherited daily) and the ROSTERED assignment (the shift-per-day schedule for the workforce whose pattern rotates — the retail floor, Chapter 4's whole subject). The mechanics the consultant wires: every active employee resolves to a shift every working day (the unassigned day is the mark the machinery cannot make — present against what? — and the assignment gap is the attendance layer's spine-with-holes), holidays and approved leave override the expectation (the absence taxonomy of Chapter 5 — the person on leave is not absent), and shift CHANGES are events with effective dates (the pattern that changed mid-month re-marks forward, never rewrites backward — the frozen-history conviction, in minutes and hours).

The overtime boundary, drawn. Where hours past the shift carry pay or lieu consequences, the attendance layer CAPTURES the hours and the policy the firm sets governs them — and the boundary discipline from module 1 applies verbatim: HR owns the captured record (the hours as facts, approved as the policy requires), the payroll function owns the computation (the rate, the statutory treatment — the accountant's terrain across the boundary). The capture rule that prevents the classic dispute: overtime is captured and APPROVED contemporaneously (the week's extra hours signed by the manager that week), because overtime reconstructed at month-end from memory is the reconstruction disease with money attached — the same week-old truth that made cash-ups daily and counts scheduled makes overtime approval weekly, and the firm that adopts it never again hosts the month-end argument about whose Saturday counted.

lessons.title: Chapter 4 — The roster: coverage, fairness & the published week
lessons.html:
For a multi-branch retail firm the roster is not an HR document — it is the machine that decides whether branches trade. This chapter is the rostering discipline: coverage first, fairness always, published ahead, changed by rule.

Coverage: the branch must open. The roster's first law is operational: every trading hour of every branch covered by the roles that hour needs (the till coverage that matches footfall — the Saturday double-cover the retail week demands; the storekeeper presence that receiving days require — the delivery calendar of Inventory 6 read INTO the roster; the opening and closing shifts held by people authorised for the till count and the cash-up — the roster meeting Accounts 3's session custody). Rostering therefore starts from the branch's DEMAND SHAPE (trading hours, peak days, delivery days, market days) and staffs it — not from staff preferences rationalised into a schedule — and the branch manager owns that fit, with HR owning the machinery that records it. The coverage read the roster must answer at a glance: any uncovered hour, any single-point day (the one keyholder whose absence closes the branch — the roster's own two-names law: critical capabilities rostered in pairs across the week, so no single absence stops trade).

Fairness: rotation by design. The unpopular shifts — the Saturdays, the closings, the market-day dawns — rotate by VISIBLE rule, because rotation by memory becomes rotation by favouritism within a quarter (the register's politics, rostered): the rotation pattern written (everyone's Saturday share explicit), exceptions governed (the standing accommodation — the parent's school run, the worshipper's day — granted deliberately, recorded, and priced into the pattern so the remaining rotation stays fair), and the roster's fairness AUDITABLE (the shift-share read per person per quarter — the number that answers the corridor grievance with data: module 8's analytics carrying it). Fairness here is not softness; it is retention economics — the roster that quietly overloads its most reliable people teaches them to become less reliable or leave, and either lesson costs more than the rotation rule.

Published ahead, changed by rule. The roster is PUBLISHED — visibly, in advance by a stated horizon (the fortnight ahead as the working norm; the week ahead as the floor) — because staff plan lives around shifts, and the roster that appears Friday night for Monday is a turnover machine wearing a schedule. Changes after publication follow the change rule: SWAPS are employee-initiated, approved (the swap request as a document — both parties, the manager's approval riding the spine, the coverage check automatic: the swap that leaves Saturday uncovered doesn't approve), and RESHUFFLES by management are events with notice and reasons (the emergency re-cover is real; the habitual reshuffle is planning failure billed to staff goodwill). Leave integrates ahead of publication (module 4's approved leave blocks the slot BEFORE the roster is cut — the leave calendar and the roster as one planning surface), and the no-show triggers the day-of protocol (the coverage fallback list, then the absence machinery of Chapter 5 — operations first, process next).

The roster as record. The published roster is retained as history — because it is the EXPECTATION side of every attendance judgment (late against what? absent from what?), and disputes are settled by what was published, not what is remembered: the roster archive is to attendance what the price list's history was to the selling track — the reference that makes every downstream record interpretable, kept by the machinery, forever.

lessons.title: Chapter 5 — Lateness, absence & regularisation
lessons.html:
The marks the machinery makes — late, absent, half-day — and the taxonomy and correction flows that keep them honest. The judgment chapter.

The absence taxonomy. Not everything away is absent, and the marks must say which: on approved leave (module 4's document — the expectation overridden, no absence exists), on holiday (the holiday list — Chapter's payroll boundary needs the distinction), off-roster (not scheduled — the part-timer's Tuesday is nobody's absence), absent (rostered, no capture, no leave — the mark that carries consequences), and the half-day and late gradations between. The taxonomy's discipline is that each category has its DOCUMENT or its LIST behind it (the leave application, the holiday list, the published roster) — an absence mark is therefore always a derived fact (expected by the roster, uncovered by any document, unattended by any capture), which is what makes it defensible when it matters (module 7's processes will stand on these marks; marks that were moods will not stand).

Lateness: policy, evenly. The late mark runs on the shift's grace (Chapter 3), and the policy layer above it is written and even: what accumulating lateness triggers (the informal word at the pattern's start, the documented conversation at its persistence, the disciplinary machinery at its refusal — Chapter 6's escalation path), and what it never does (the ad-hoc docking of pay improvised at a supervisor's desk — consequences run through POLICY and, where they touch pay, through the payroll boundary with the employment framework's blessing, because improvised deductions are grievance and liability material at once). The evenness conviction repeats because it is the layer's whole credibility: the grace and the policy apply identically from the newest till assistant to the branch manager — the attendance system that visibly binds the senior binds everyone, and the one that visibly exempts them binds no one.

Regularisation: the correction with a document. The employee-side correction flow for capture's honest gaps — the forgotten badge, the dead phone, the offsite morning at the supplier: the attendance regularisation request, raised by the employee against the specific day, reasoned, and approved along the spine (the manager who can see the day's reality), landing as a corrected mark that is VISIBLY a regularisation (the audit trail keeping capture and correction distinguishable forever). The governance that keeps the flow honest: regularisation is bounded in TIME (raised within days, not batched at month-end when memory has composed itself), bounded in VOLUME (the person regularising weekly has a capture problem or a candour problem — the read flags both), and never a substitute for capture (the branch where regularisation is routine has let the machinery fail politely — Chapter 2's maintenance alarm, employee edition).

The no-show protocol. The rostered absence, live: the day-of sequence — coverage first (Chapter 4's fallback list; the branch trades), contact attempted and LOGGED (the welfare dimension is real: the no-show is sometimes an emergency, and the firm that calls before it judges is both humane and evidentially sound), and the mark plus the follow-up on return (the explanation heard, the leave document raised retroactively where the reason warrants and policy allows, or the absence standing with its conversation — Chapter 6's path). The pattern the protocol prevents: the absence that fades into assumption (module 1's ghost was born exactly this way) — every rostered no-show resolves to a category within days, by process, and the attendance record ends every month with no unexplained days: the layer's own suspense-account sweep, at human scale.

lessons.title: Chapter 6 — The attendance reads & the discipline boundary
lessons.html:
Captured attendance becomes management only when read — and read into a fair escalation path, never an ambush. The reading chapter, and the boundary where attendance meets discipline.

The monthly attendance read. The standing page, per branch and per person: attendance rate (days present against rostered), punctuality rate (on-time against expected), absence days by category (the taxonomy paying off — approved leave is not a blemish; unexplained absence is a signal), regularisation counts (the capture-health overlay), and overtime hours where captured. Read the academy's way: TREND before level (the person whose punctuality walked from 96% to 84% over a quarter is a story; the steady 90% may be the shift design), COMPARE like with like (branches against their own patterns — the market-day branch's earliness profile differs by design), and DECOMPOSE before concluding (the branch whose lateness spiked in June may have a new till assistant, a changed bus route, or a device that drifted five minutes — the read tells you to find out which, not what you'll find).

The patterns worth naming. The reads surface the classics every branch manager recognises once shown: the Monday pattern (the absences that cluster on the weekend's far side), the payday pattern, the closing-shift fade (the early exits that cluster on cash-up nights — a read that belongs beside Accounts 3's session data, because the two together answer whether the fade is fatigue or avoidance), and the pre-resignation drift (the attendance decay that precedes the letter — the signal module 7's retention conversations want early, not posthumously). The reading discipline for all of them: patterns are QUESTIONS, not verdicts — the Monday pattern has explanations from transport to caregiving to disengagement, and the read's output is a conversation, which is the boundary's whole design.

The escalation path: read → conversation → process. The boundary between attendance data and disciplinary consequence, built as a path with stages: the READ surfaces the pattern (data, not accusation); the CONVERSATION happens first and informally (the manager's I've noticed — what's going on? — documented as held, not as charges: most patterns end here, because most patterns have reasons, and the firm that asks first fixes transport problems instead of prosecuting them); the DOCUMENTED stage follows only persistence (the formal conversation with its note, the expectation and timeline written — module 7's machinery beginning, with the attendance record as its evidence base); and the PROCESS stage is module 7's proper terrain (warnings, the disciplinary procedure, the employment framework's requirements — never improvised at this module's altitude). The rule that names the chapter: never ambush — the person who first learns of their attendance problem at the appraisal, or worse the termination meeting, has been failed by every stage of this path, and the failure is the firm's: data that was read and never raised is not evidence of process; it is evidence of its absence. The path's fairness is also its effectiveness — the pattern raised at week three changes behaviour; the same pattern raised at month nine changes lawyers.

The reads' other customers. Before the boundary chapter closes, the reminder that attendance reads serve more than discipline: the roster design (the coverage that keeps failing Saturdays is a staffing-level fact), the shift policy (the grace that everyone misses by four minutes is a bus-timetable fact), the wellbeing lens (the reliable person whose pattern breaks is a check-in, not a case), and module 5's appraisals (attendance as one evidence stream among the operational reads — context, never the whole story). The layer reads people; the reader stays a manager, not a magistrate.

lessons.title: Chapter 7 — The payroll boundary: the attendance close & handoff
lessons.html:
Module 1 drew the boundary — HR owns the inputs payroll consumes — and attendance is the largest input crossing it. This chapter is the handoff's machinery: the monthly attendance close, the package handed across, and the disagreement disease it prevents.

The attendance close. The month's attendance is FINALISED — a close, run with the discipline Accounts 7 taught, at people scale: the close date fixed (aligned with the payroll calendar the accountant owns — the attendance cutoff that payroll's timetable can rely on, month after month), the pre-close sweep run (unexplained absences resolved to categories — Chapter 5's protocol completing; pending regularisations decided, not carried; orphan events closed; manual marks reviewed), the marks then LOCKED for the period (corrections after the close exist but are exceptions with documents — the frozen-period conviction, in attendance clothes: the March that changes silently in May breaks every downstream number that read it), and the close's completion logged (the month, the closer, the date — the ritual with a name).

The handoff package. What crosses the boundary, itemised: days worked per person (against the roster's expected days), absence days BY CATEGORY (the taxonomy's payoff — payroll treats approved leave, unpaid absence, and half-days differently, and the categories carry the treatment), lateness data where policy attaches consequences (through policy, never improvisation — Chapter 5's conviction restated at the handoff), overtime hours as captured and approved (the computation staying on payroll's side), and the leave interface (module 4's balances and takings — the preview this chapter leaves for the next module). The package's form matters less than its properties: COMPLETE (every active employee accounted — the module-1 status discipline making 'active' a true list), CATEGORISED (no ambiguous days), and FINAL (the close's lock making it citable — payroll computes once, from one version).

The disagreement disease. The failure this machinery prevents, described because every consultant will meet it: HR and payroll disagreeing about March — the salary computed from one attendance version while HR's records say another, discovered when an employee disputes a deduction, escalating into an archaeology of registers, memories, and versions. The disease's anatomy is always the same: no close (attendance perpetually editable), no categories (absences ambiguous), no single package (payroll assembling its own attendance from side channels), and the cure is exactly this chapter: one close, one package, one version — after which the employee's dispute has a clean answer path (the record shown, the regularisation flow if the record is wrong, the correction as a documented exception if proven — the dispute resolved by machinery instead of negotiation, which is the whole track in one sentence).

The boundary's rhythm. The handoff joins the calendars: the attendance close on HR's monthly calendar (module 8 will seat it), the package's delivery on the payroll calendar's dependency line (the accountant's payroll run waits on it, by design and by date), and the boundary MEETING where scale warrants one (the monthly ten minutes where HR and the payroll function confirm the package landed and the exceptions were understood — the two functions meshing on schedule instead of colliding in disputes). The boundary managed this way is invisible; unmanaged, it is where the people layer and the money layer grind — and the consultant who wires it has prevented the most common HR-adjacent dispute in the trade.

lessons.title: Chapter 8 — Case study: HealthTrade's working rhythm
lessons.html:
The attendance layer, installed across three branches and a head office. Every chapter clocks in.

The capture rollout (Ch. 1-2). Devices mounted at the three branches and the distribution unit; mobile check-in configured for the two drivers and the field salesperson; desk sessions for head office. The introduction done the protections way — the branch meetings where the pitch is fairness (your punctuality becomes visible; the register's politics end) — and adoption lands in three weeks with one wobble: week two's capture-health read shows Ibadan's manual-mark share climbing; the device, not the people — a power issue at the door socket, fixed same week, the read having done exactly its job (the maintenance alarm, not the workaround culture).

Shifts and the roster (Ch. 3-4). The shift set defined from the trading calendar with the branch managers: opening and closing shifts wrapped around the till count and cash-up windows, the Saturday double-cover, and Akure's market-day dawn shift aligned to the delivery run (the Inventory 6 run calendar and the roster now describing the same Tuesday). Rosters published a fortnight ahead on the visible board and the phones; the rotation rule written (Saturday share explicit per person); one standing accommodation recorded (a school-run start moved thirty minutes, priced into the pattern). The coverage read catches a single-point day at Akure — the only closing-authorised person on Thursdays — fixed by authorising and rostering a second closer: the roster's two-names law, applied before the absence that would have closed the branch early.

The flows, live (Ch. 5). The first month's regularisations run through the spine — a forgotten badge, a supplier-visit morning — approved in a day, visibly marked. The no-show protocol fires once: a till assistant absent on a rostered Saturday; coverage from the fallback list inside the hour (the branch trades), contact logged (a family emergency — the retroactive leave document raised per policy on return, the absence resolving to its true category within three days). The month ends with zero unexplained days — the suspense sweep, human edition.

The read and the path (Ch. 6). Month two's attendance read surfaces the classic: a warehouse assistant's absences clustering on Mondays — four in eight weeks. The path runs as designed: the data goes to the branch manager as a question, not a verdict; the informal conversation finds a transport reality (a Monday market route that doubles his commute); the fix is operational, not disciplinary (his rostered pattern shifts to a later Monday start within the shift set, the rotation adjusted fairly) — and the pattern ends. The debrief note the consultant files for the owner is the chapter's thesis in one line: the read found it in week eight; the register would have found it at the appraisal — as an accusation instead of a bus route.

The first attendance close (Ch. 7). Month one's close runs on the fixed date: the pre-close sweep resolves the categories (the Saturday emergency already documented; two pending regularisations decided), the marks lock, and the package crosses the boundary — days worked, absences by category, one approved overtime batch — on the payroll calendar's dependency date. The accountant's note back is the boundary working: computed from one version, no queries. Three branches, one rhythm, and the attendance layer joins the firm's calendar with its close owned and its reads scheduled — the working heartbeat the leave module will now write its documents against.

lessons.title: Chapter 9 — Common mistakes & the third law
lessons.html:
The attendance layer's scar tissue. Symptom → disease → fix.

Pattern 1 — the paper register. Symptom: the exercise book at the counter; self-reported times; pages that answer to the pen's holder. Disease: reconstruction instead of capture (Ch. 1) — the record written after the fact by interested parties. Fix: capture at the moment by a mechanism the person doesn't author, introduced on the protections framing, with the register retired the same week the device works.

Pattern 2 — the proxy check-in. Symptom: badges lent, PINs shared, the friend who clocks two people in; capture that says present for the absent. Disease: the capture method that delegates (Ch. 2) — and an introduction that framed the system as adversary, making gaming feel fair. Fix: biometric capture for threshold roles, the location rules for mobile check-in, the orphan-and-pattern reads that surface proxies — and the culture repair that outlasts all three: the protections re-taught, and the proxy treated as the serious integrity matter it is (module 7's process, not a shrug), because a capture layer known to be gameable is the register with a power cable.

Pattern 3 — the roster in someone's head. Symptom: shifts announced verbally, changed nightly; staff learning their Saturday on Friday; disputes with no published reference. Disease: expectation without record (Ch. 4). Fix: the published roster on its horizon, changes by the swap-and-reshuffle rules, the archive retained — the expectation side of every attendance judgment made citable.

Pattern 4 — regularisation as routine. Symptom: correction requests outnumbering exceptions; month-end batches of remembered days; a capture layer everyone politely bypasses. Disease: the machinery failed and nobody escalated (Ch. 2, 5) — or the bounds were never set. Fix: the time and volume bounds enforced, the capture-health read weekly, devices fixed as operations priorities (the branch door's device is trading infrastructure), and the routine regulariser's conversation held.

Pattern 5 — the ambush. Symptom: attendance data surfacing for the first time at the appraisal or the termination; the person who never knew there was a pattern. Disease: data read but never raised (Ch. 6) — the path's stages skipped. Fix: the monthly read with the conversation-first path, the documented stages in order, and the conviction restated: data never raised is not evidence of process; it is evidence of its absence.

Pattern 6 — the perpetual March. Symptom: HR and payroll disagreeing about a month neither can reconstruct; attendance edited silently after salaries ran; disputes settled by negotiation. Disease: no close, no categories, no single package (Ch. 7). Fix: the attendance close on its date, the locked marks, the one handoff package — and the boundary meeting where scale warrants.

The third law. The first law made the record; the second governed how people enter; the third governs the daily truth: attendance is captured, not remembered — presence recorded at the moment by mechanisms nobody authors, judged against published shifts and rosters, corrected only by documented flows, read into conversations before processes, and closed monthly into one package the payroll boundary can trust. The capture protects the punctual, the roster keeps the branch trading, the taxonomy keeps the marks honest, and the close keeps March meaning March forever. Module 4 takes the taxonomy's biggest category and gives it its own machinery: leave — the entitlement managed, not the favour negotiated.

leave.title: HR 4 — Leave Management
leave.desc: The entitlement managed, not the favour negotiated: leave types on the Nigerian statutory floor, policies and allocation by structure, the application on the spine, the balance as a ledger with its liability view, holiday lists and the amendment flow, leave planning against the trading year with blackouts and encashment governance, and the special situations from maternity to abandonment.

lessons.title: Chapter 1 — Leave: the entitlement managed, not the favour negotiated
lessons.html:
Module 3's taxonomy had one category too big for a paragraph: approved leave. This module gives it its machinery — and opens with the thesis that reframes how most trading firms think about it: leave is an entitlement managed, not a favour negotiated.

The two diseases. Unstructured leave fails in two opposite directions, and the consultant meets both in the same week: leave as favour — the request granted by mood and standing, where the supervisor's friends holiday and the quiet workers don't ask, where nobody knows their balance because there IS no balance, only negotiations — the register's politics (module 3) applied to rest, corroding fairness exactly where the workforce watches most closely; and leave unmanaged — the opposite failure, where leave is technically granted but structurally untaken: no planning, no encouragement, no tracking, and the firm quietly accrues both a financial LIABILITY (untaken leave is money owed — Chapter 5's ledger makes it visible) and a human one (the exhausted workforce, and the never-absent employee Chapter 10 will name as one of the trade's classic fraud tells). The cure for both is the same machinery: entitlements defined by policy, balances kept as a ledger, applications as documents riding the spine, and planning that meets the roster — the module's map.

The entitlement frame. The reframe the consultant teaches owners, because it changes every downstream conversation: leave is not a gift the firm dispenses; it is part of the EMPLOYMENT BARGAIN — earned by service, defined by policy sitting on a statutory floor (Chapter 2), and owed as surely as salary. The firm's discretion lives in WHERE policy sets the offer above the floor and WHEN leave is taken (the scheduling conversation — Chapter 7's coverage tension is real and legitimate), never in WHETHER the entitlement exists. The frame pays immediately: the manager who understands leave as owed schedules it; the one who understands it as a favour hoards it — and hoarded leave becomes December's collapse (Chapter 7) and the balance-sheet liability the accountant will eventually price (Chapter 5).

The coverage tension, named honestly. The trading firm's legitimate anxiety, stated at the door so the module can answer it: the branch must trade (module 3's roster law), and leave removes rostered capacity — so the entitlement and the coverage pull against each other, and the resolution is neither denial (the favour disease) nor chaos (everyone gone in December) but PLANNING: leave spread deliberately across the year, visible on the calendar managers roster from, approved with the coverage check, and protected by the blackout rules the trade's peaks genuinely justify (Chapter 7). A firm that plans leave trades every day AND rests its people — the tension is managed, not won — and the module's machinery exists precisely to make that management routine instead of heroic.

lessons.title: Chapter 2 — Leave types & the Nigerian statutory floor
lessons.html:
The taxonomy, and the layer of law beneath it. The consultant's altitude here mirrors the tax module's: know the FLOOR exists and roughly where it sits, configure the policy the firm sets ABOVE it, and route the law's reading to the employment adviser who owns it.

The statutory floor, at working altitude. Nigerian employment law sets minimums the firm's policy cannot undercut for the workers the law covers: annual leave — the Labour Act's entitlement after twelve months of continuous service (the statutory minimum for ordinary workers is famously modest — six working days — which is precisely why Chapter's second half matters: market practice offers well above it, and the floor is a floor, not a benchmark); sick leave — the Act's provision for paid sick absence (up to twelve working days a year, on the conditions the Act sets, medical certification among them); maternity leave — the protected leave the Act guarantees (twelve weeks, with the pay provision the Act attaches and the dismissal protections around it — the area where employer error is most expensive and most scrutinised); and the surrounding rules (public holidays as paid days, the timing and pay-in-lieu constraints) the adviser confirms. The consultant's discipline, verbatim from the tax module: these numbers are the ORIENTATION, not the advice — the Act's coverage definitions, its exceptions, and the reform landscape are the employment adviser's terrain, and the policy page records what the adviser confirmed, dated, reviewed annually.

The firm's types. The working set a Nigerian trading firm configures: annual leave (the core entitlement, set at the firm's policy level — commonly well above the floor, graded by seniority where the firm chooses), sick leave (with its certification rules — Chapter 4), maternity leave (the statutory shape, run properly — Chapter 8), casual leave (the short-notice personal-matters allowance many firms offer — small, bounded, and distinct from annual so the annual entitlement stays plannable), compassionate leave (bereavement — defined, so the worst weeks of people's lives are not also negotiations), examination/study leave (where the firm supports development — module 6's terrain meeting this one), and leave without pay (the governed exception — Chapter 8). Each type a configured record: its entitlement, its accrual, its notice rules, its documentation requirements, its pay treatment flagged for the boundary.

Floor versus policy: the design conversation. The chapter's central distinction, taught with the owner in the room: the LAW sets what the firm must do; the POLICY sets what the firm chooses to do — and the choice is a labour-market position, not a compliance question. The firm competing for good storekeepers and accountants against the market's practice offers the market's leave or explains itself at every offer stage; the firm resting on the statutory six days is technically compliant and commercially noticeable. The policy page records the choices per type and grade, the adviser's confirmation of the floor beneath them, and the review date — and the configuration then ENFORCES the policy evenly (the system granting what the page says, to everyone the page covers), which is the entitlement frame made mechanical: the offer is the offer, for everyone, visibly.

lessons.title: Chapter 3 — Policies & allocation: granting the entitlement
lessons.html:
The policy becomes days in a balance through ALLOCATION — the machinery that grants entitlements per person per period, prorated at the edges, governed at the carry-over. The granting chapter.

The policy attaches by structure. Module 1's architecture pays off again: leave policies attach by GRADE and type (the grade's annual entitlement — the band structure carrying its first benefit), by employment TYPE (the full-timer's entitlement versus the part-timer's proportion versus the contractor's contract terms — module 1's type field driving policy exactly as promised), and by tenure rules where the policy sets them (the entitlement that steps up at year three). The attachment discipline: policy lives in the CONFIGURATION, not in per-person edits — the individually adjusted entitlement is the favour disease wearing an admin screen, and exceptions above policy are policy CHANGES (versioned, dated, applied to the class) or documented individual terms (the contract that genuinely differs), never quiet numbers.

Allocation mechanics. The grant itself, per period: the ANNUAL allocation (the year's entitlement granted at the period's start — simple, plannable, the small firm's default) versus ACCRUAL (the entitlement earned monthly as service accrues — the method that matches the earning to the year and simplifies the leaver's arithmetic, at the cost of early-year balances that constrain planning; the choice is policy, made once, applied evenly). PRORATION at the edges: the joiner's first year granted proportionally from their start (the pipeline's date-of-joining field — module 1's anchor doing this exact work), the leaver's final year prorated to their exit (module 7's full-and-final computation consuming this number across the boundary). And the allocation as a RECORD: each grant a document (person, type, period, days, basis) — because the balance Chapter 5 builds is a ledger, and ledgers are built from documents, not adjustments.

Carry-forward: the governed remainder. The year ends with balances unspent, and the policy must say what happens — the three clean answers: LAPSE (use-it-or-lose-it — maximally simple, maximally pressuring toward Chapter 7's December problem), CARRY with a CAP (the market's common middle — a bounded number of days crossing the year, the cap keeping the liability from compounding), or ENCASH (the payout for untaken days — a policy decision with real cost, computed across the payroll boundary, and governed so it doesn't become a standing salary top-up that pays people NOT to rest: Chapter 7 treats encashment properly). The governance conviction: whatever the rule, it is WRITTEN, applied evenly, and executed by the year-end allocation ritual (the carry-forward computed and granted as documents, the lapses logged, the encashments listed for the boundary) — the year boundary crossed by machinery, not by a January of arguments about what December's balances meant.

The allocation calendar. The rhythm this chapter adds to module 8's page: the annual allocation run (the new year's grants, the carry-forward execution — scheduled, owned, verified), the joiner's allocation inside the onboarding checklist (module 2's day-one readiness including the leave balance that self-service will show), and the periodic accrual run where that method rules. Allocation done this way is invisible; done by memory it is January's dispute season — the module's quiet economics.

lessons.title: Chapter 4 — The leave application: the document & the spine
lessons.html:
The entitlement is spent through a DOCUMENT — the leave application — and the document's flow is everything module 1 and 3 built, working together. The spending chapter.

The application's anatomy. The employee raises it (self-service — the join of module 1 paying its daily dividend): the type, the dates, the reason where the type asks for one, and the system's own contributions at the moment of application — the BALANCE CHECK (the application against an insufficient balance is caught at birth, not discovered in payroll: the days available shown as the form fills), the HOLIDAY overlay (the applied span netted of holidays and off-roster days per the policy's counting rules — working days versus calendar days, decided once in configuration), and the half-day option where policy offers it. The application lands in the approver's queue along the SPINE (module 1's reports-to field routing it to the person who owns the coverage consequence), and the approval or decline lands back with its reason — the whole conversation a document trail, which is the point: the leave that was 'agreed in the corridor' and never recorded is module 3's absence-mark dispute waiting to happen.

Notice: applied in advance, per type. The policy's notice rules, enforced by the flow: annual leave applied ahead by the stated horizon (the fortnight-for-a-week norm many firms use — enough for the roster to adjust; Chapter 7's planning makes long leave visible far earlier), casual leave's shorter fuse (the type exists precisely for the short-notice reality — bounded so it cannot become the annual entitlement's queue-jumping route), and the approval SLA on the firm's side (the application that sits unanswered for a week teaches people to revert to corridors — the spine's approver owns a response time, and module 8's read watches it). The evenness conviction, again: notice rules bind everyone, and the senior whose leave appears retroactively teaches the policy's real name.

Sick leave: the retroactive reality. The one type whose document follows the absence, governed accordingly: the sick absence reported on the day (the contact protocol — module 3's no-show machinery distinguishing the reported-sick from the unexplained absence from hour one), the application regularised on return within the policy's window, and the CERTIFICATION rule applied as written (the medical certificate for absences past the policy's threshold — commonly beyond two days, per the firm's policy on the statutory frame; required evenly, filed to the record). The design balance the consultant states plainly: certification thresholds exist because sick leave without any evidence rule becomes the elastic extension of every weekend, AND the rule is set humanely because demanding paperwork for every single day taxes the genuinely ill and the clinic queues — the policy's number is a trust calibration, made once, applied evenly, reviewed against Chapter 10's pattern reads rather than adjusted per suspicion.

Cancellations and changes. The lifecycle's edges: the approved leave cancelled before it starts (the document reversed, the balance restored, the roster released — by flow, not deletion), the leave cut short by recall (the genuine operational emergency — governed: the recall is a management decision with a name on it, the untaken days restored, and the pattern read, because the firm that habitually recalls has a planning disease wearing an urgency costume), and the extension mid-leave (a fresh application against the balance, decided on coverage like any other). Every edge a document; the balance ledger of Chapter 5 always reconciling to the trail.

lessons.title: Chapter 5 — Balances & the leave ledger
lessons.html:
Behind every application sits the number that governs it: the BALANCE — and this chapter builds it properly, as a ledger, because that is what it is. The accounting chapter of the people track.

The ledger grammar, applied to days. The balance is not a field someone edits; it is a RUNNING LEDGER per person per leave type: allocations CREDIT it (Chapter 3's documents), approved applications DEBIT it (Chapter 4's), cancellations reverse, carry-forwards credit the new year, encashments debit against their payout, and the balance at any moment is the ledger's sum — never an adjusted number, always a derived one. Every conviction from the money tracks transfers verbatim: the balance that doesn't reconcile to its documents is a broken ledger (find the undocumented movement — it exists); adjustments are exceptions with reasons (the correction document, visible forever); and history is frozen (last year's ledger is sealed by the year-end ritual — the January argument about December's balance is answered by pointing, not remembering). The consultant who has taught four tracks of ledgers teaches this one in ten minutes, and the accountant in the room smiles: it is the same grammar, denominated in days.

Visibility: the self-service dividend. The balance SHOWN — each employee seeing their own, per type, with the ledger behind it (the allocations and takings listed — the transparency that answers why is my balance 11? with a trail instead of a negotiation) — is module 1's biggest single query-killer: the balance question, asked of HR in every unstructured firm weekly, simply stops existing. Managers see their TEAM's balances (the spine defining visibility as always — the coverage planner needs to know who is carrying 18 days into Q4: Chapter 7's planning read starts here), and HR sees the population (the distribution read: the balances clustering high are Chapter 7's planning failure ripening; the negative outliers are governance leaks).

Negative balances: the governed edge. The policy question the configuration must answer: may leave be taken beyond the balance? The clean default is NO (the balance check refusing at application — the entitlement spent as earned), with the governed exception where policy allows it (the advance against the next allocation — bounded in days, approved above the spine's first level, and recorded as the negative ledger position it is, because an ungoverned negative balance is a loan nobody priced: the leaver with minus-eight days is a full-and-final deduction conversation module 7 will have to host, and the policy should have had it first).

The liability view: the accountant's interest. The chapter's boundary-crossing insight, taught because it converts owners: untaken leave is not just a wellbeing datum — it is a FINANCIAL LIABILITY (days owed that will be paid, as leave or as encashment or in the leaver's final settlement), and the accrued-leave provision is a balance-sheet line the accountant computes from THIS ledger (Accounts 4's provision discipline, fed by HR's data — the boundary handoff's quiet second passenger). The read that follows: the leave liability trended (the firm whose balances compound yearly is deferring a cost and calling it flexibility), per branch and grade (where the hoarding lives), and priced (the accountant's valuation making the wellbeing conversation a naira conversation — the language owners hear fastest). The ledger built this chapter serves three masters at once — the employee's clarity, the manager's planning, the accountant's provision — which is what a master data layer is FOR, and why the notebook it replaces (Chapter 10's pattern) failed all three.

lessons.title: Chapter 6 — Holiday lists & the calendar
lessons.html:
The year's shared days off — the holiday list — small machinery with outsized reach, because every attendance expectation and leave computation reads it. The calendar chapter.

The holiday list as a record. Per year, per applicable population: the list of public holidays (the Nigerian federal set — the two Eids, Christmas and Easter's days, Independence Day, New Year, Workers' Day, Democracy Day — plus the state-declared days where branches sit in states that observe them: the branch-specific list is real machinery for the multi-state firm, and module 1's branch field is what it attaches by), created ANNUALLY as a ritual (the year's list drafted from the known calendar, adopted, published — module 8's calendar carries the task) and AMENDED as declarations land — because the Nigerian reality the consultant plans for is that holidays are sometimes declared or moved days in advance (the lunar-calendar holidays confirmed on sighting; the government's occasional additions), and the amendment flow (the list updated, the affected rosters adjusted, the workforce notified through the standing channel) is the difference between a calendar quirk and a payroll dispute.

What the list wires into. The reach, itemised: ATTENDANCE expectations (module 3's taxonomy — the holiday is not an absence; the marked day resolves against the list automatically), LEAVE computation (Chapter 4's netting — the leave span crossing a holiday doesn't spend the holiday, per the policy's counting rule), the ROSTER (the trading firm's honest complication: retail often TRADES on public holidays — the branch open on a holiday staffs by the holiday-working policy the firm sets, with the premium or lieu-day treatment the policy defines and the payroll boundary computes; the roster for a trading holiday is planned like a Saturday, and the fairness machinery of module 3's rotation covers who works it), and the PAYROLL boundary (holiday pay treatments crossing with the attendance package — the categories carrying the treatment, as always).

The optional-holiday pattern. Where firms observe it — the restricted or optional holiday (the day granted to those who observe it, worked by those who don't, commonly around religious observances the workforce splits across): configured as its own small type or list flag, governed evenly (the observance taken at the employee's declaration, not the supervisor's assessment), and rostered with the same coverage logic as everything else. The point is not the pattern's universality — many firms simply use the federal list — but the consultant's readiness: the multi-faith workforce is the Nigerian trading floor's normal condition, and the firm that handles observance by policy handles it without friction; the one that handles it by negotiation rehearses the favour disease at its most sensitive point.

The calendar as shared surface. The closing frame: the holiday list, the leave calendar (Chapter 7), and the roster (module 3) are three views of ONE planning surface — the year as the firm will actually work it — and the implementation that publishes them together (the branch's wall and phone showing the same truth) has made the working year legible to everyone who lives inside it. Legibility is the quiet product: the workforce that can SEE the year plans against it, and half of Chapter 7's discipline happens by itself.

lessons.title: Chapter 7 — Leave planning, coverage & encashment
lessons.html:
The module's operational summit: leave meets the roster, and the tension Chapter 1 named gets its machinery. Planning, the coverage check, the blackout rules, and the encashment governance.

The leave calendar. The manager's planning surface: approved and pending leave visible across the team and the months (the spine defining the view), read TOGETHER with the roster (module 3's coverage law consuming this exact data — the approved leave blocks the slot BEFORE the roster is cut), and consulted at approval (the coverage check as part of the decision, not an afterthought: the application whose dates leave Saturday uncovered comes back with the honest conversation — these dates strand the branch; these alternatives don't — which is the entitlement honoured AND the branch trading: the tension managed in one screen).

Spreading the year: the planning conversation. The proactive half — because approval-time checks manage requests, and planning PREVENTS the crunch: the annual leave-planning conversation (early in the year, per team: entitlements on the table, preferences gathered, the year sketched — the December-heavy trade's staff steered toward the January-October window with the honesty that December is the trade's harvest), the quarterly balance read (Chapter 5's manager view — the person carrying 18 days into Q4 gets the nudge in September, not the collision in December), and the use-it culture the firm deliberately builds: leave ENCOURAGED, modelled by seniors (the manager who never rests teaches the team that rest is weakness — and hoards the liability), and protected (the approved leave that gets cancelled by habitual 'emergencies' teaches people not to plan, which re-manufactures the December rush the planning existed to prevent).

Blackouts: the peak protected, honestly. The trading calendar's legitimate claim: the windows where the trade cannot spare capacity (the December retail peak, the season's harvest weeks, the stock-count dates of Inventory 4 — the events the year is built around), declared as BLACKOUT or restricted windows in policy — announced at the year's start (not sprung in November), applied evenly (the blackout that binds the floor but not the office is the favour disease with a calendar), bounded (the blackout is weeks, not quarters — the restriction that swallows a third of the year is a staffing-level problem wearing a policy), and COMPENSATED in spirit (the December worker gets January's first pick — the rotation fairness of module 3, applied to the year). Emergency leave inside a blackout remains what it always is — the compassionate and sick realities don't read calendars — and the policy says so, so the blackout constrains planning, never humanity.

Encashment: the governed payout. The policy question with money attached: paying for untaken days. The governance the consultant configures: encashment as a BOUNDED exception (the cap on encashable days — commonly the carry-forward's excess or a stated maximum — not an open market where the workforce sells its rest back annually), PRICED across the boundary (the computation is payroll's — the rate basis the accountant owns; HR's ledger supplies the days), and READ for what it reveals (the encashment list is the planning-failure report wearing a payout: the same names yearly means those roles cannot release their people, which is a coverage-design finding, not a payments routine). The design conviction stated for owners who like encashment's simplicity: systematically paying people not to rest optimises the liability and abandons the wellbeing — the entitlement's point was the rest; the payout is the exception that keeps the ledger honest at the edges, and the firm that finds itself encashing broadly should fix its planning, not enlarge its budget.

lessons.title: Chapter 8 — Special situations: the governed edges
lessons.html:
The leave layer's hard cases — the situations where governance matters most because stakes, law, and humanity converge. The edges chapter, at consultant altitude with the adviser's boundary bright.

Maternity leave, run properly. The statutory shape (twelve weeks with the Act's pay provision and its protections — the adviser confirms the current reading and any state variations), and the PROCESS the firm wraps around it, which is where implementations differ: the notification handled with the confidentiality module 1's custody frame demands, the leave planned EARLY (the known start window makes cover planning a months-ahead exercise, not a scramble — the cover plan documented: who holds the till authority, the warehouse custody, the approval roles during the absence, which is the academy's handover discipline applied to a planned absence), the return handled deliberately (the return date confirmed, the role held as the law requires, the re-entry supported — the returning employee finding their access intact and their desk expected is module 2's day-one readiness, second edition), and the record trail complete throughout — because this is the leave category where employer missteps carry the heaviest legal and reputational weight, and process is protection for everyone.

Extended sick leave. Beyond the certification threshold into the long absence: the escalating documentation the policy defines (the certificates' cadence, the medical review at the stated milestone), the pay treatment steps the policy sets on the statutory frame (full, then the policy's reduced provisions — the adviser's terrain, the configuration's enforcement), the contact discipline (the welfare check-ins that are support, scheduled and logged — the long-absent employee who never hears from the firm learns what they were worth), and the eventual capability question where recovery stalls (the process the employment framework governs strictly — module 7's terrain, never improvised here beyond the note that it EXISTS and is a process, not a deletion).

Leave without pay. The governed exception: granted by policy's criteria (the exhausted balance with genuine need; the extended personal circumstance), approved above the spine's first level (the unpaid month is a bigger decision than a leave day), bounded in duration, and crossed to the boundary correctly (the unpaid days in the attendance package's categories — the treatment payroll applies is exactly why the taxonomy exists). The governance point: LWOP as a safety valve is humane; LWOP as a routine channel is a symptom (the entitlement too small, the planning failed, or the attendance machinery leaking — the read tells which).

Study leave & the development bond. Where module 6's development machinery meets this one: the study leave policy (what the firm supports, at what pay, with what evidence of enrolment and progress), and the BOND concept at consultant altitude — the service commitment some firms attach to sponsored study (the agreement the adviser drafts and the firm applies evenly; the consultant's job is the record: the bond's terms filed, its dates tracked by module 1's expiry machinery, its status visible at separation when module 7's full-and-final asks).

The boundary distinctions. The edges where leave meets other machinery, kept crisp: leave during NOTICE (module 7's rules — commonly constrained by policy so notice periods serve their purpose; the balance's fate resolved in the final settlement), leave versus ABANDONMENT (module 1's ghost revisited with its process — the unexplained extended absence walked through the contact protocol and the documented abandonment procedure, never a quiet status flip), and SUSPENSION versus leave (module 7's disciplinary machinery is not a leave type — the distinction that keeps both records honest). Every edge, a document; every document, the adviser-confirmed process behind it — the chapter's whole method in one line.

lessons.title: Chapter 9 — Case study: HealthTrade's leave layer
lessons.html:
The entitlement machinery, installed. Every chapter clocks in.

Policy and allocation (Ch. 2-3). The design sessions with the employment adviser and the MD: annual leave set well above the floor (graded — 15 working days at grade 1 rising to 21 at grade 3; the market-position conversation held explicitly: we hire against firms offering this), sick leave on the statutory frame with the two-day certification threshold, casual leave at four bounded days, compassionate defined, and the policy page signed and dated with the adviser's floor confirmation attached. Allocation runs annual-grant with joiner proration; carry-forward capped at five days; the year-end ritual scheduled. The allocations run as documents — 27 grants, each a record — and self-service shows every balance by week's end: the balance-question emails stop within the month, as promised.

The flows, live (Ch. 4-5). The applications ride the spine with the balance check at birth; the first decline is instructive — a storekeeper's dates stranding a delivery-day Tuesday, returned with alternatives, re-applied and approved in a day (the tension managed, visibly fairly). A negative-balance request (a grade-1 assistant, three days short, family obligation) is handled by the written advance rule: approved one level up, bounded, recorded as the ledger position it is. The sick-leave certification rule meets its first test evenly: a four-day absence certificated and filed — the same rule, the following month, for a supervisor: the evenness noticed, as it always is.

The calendar and the peak (Ch. 6-7). The holiday list adopted in January; the Eid confirmation lands three days ahead and the amendment flow runs cleanly (list updated, two rosters adjusted, the announcement through the standing channel — a calendar quirk, not a dispute). The December blackout is declared in FEBRUARY with its honest framing (December is our harvest; January's first pick goes to December's workers) — and the leave-planning conversations spread the year visibly: the Q3 balance read catches two heavy carriers, nudged in September, resting in October. December trades fully staffed for the first time in the firm's memory; January's first-pick list honours the promise, publicly.

The maternity case (Ch. 8). Mid-year, the Ibadan senior till operator: notification handled with the custody discipline, the twelve weeks planned four months ahead — the cover plan documented (till authority delegated to the named second, the Saturday roster re-rotated, the approval role remapped for the duration), the adviser's pay-provision reading applied through the boundary, check-ins scheduled and logged, and the return prepared (access intact, the role held, the first week's roster eased). The debrief line in the file: the process protected everyone — including the firm.

The liability read (Ch. 5, 7). Year-end, the boundary's quiet second passenger: HR's ledger hands the accountant the accrued-leave position; the provision computes at ₦1.9m — trended DOWN from the pre-system estimate (the planning spread having converted hoarded days into taken rest), with the encashment list at three names, each explained (the cap's excess, priced and paid through payroll). The MD's year-note joins the collection: we used to negotiate rest; now we plan it — and it costs less. The leave layer ends its first year with balances that reconcile, a December that traded, and the entitlement visibly the same for everyone — which was the thesis, delivered.

lessons.title: Chapter 10 — Common mistakes & the fourth law
lessons.html:
The leave layer's scar tissue. Symptom → disease → fix.

Pattern 1 — leave as favour. Symptom: the supervisor's friends holiday; the quiet workers don't ask; no balances, only negotiations. Disease: the entitlement dispensed by mood (Ch. 1) — the register's politics applied to rest. Fix: policy by grade and type, allocation as documents, applications on the spine, and the evenness that binds seniors first — the offer is the offer, for everyone, visibly.

Pattern 2 — the December collapse. Symptom: half the branch applying for the peak; approvals by seniority scramble; the branch trading short in its harvest month. Disease: no planning, no blackout, no year-spreading (Ch. 7). Fix: the blackout declared in February with its compensating first-pick, the annual planning conversation, the quarterly balance nudges — the year spread by machinery.

Pattern 3 — balances in a notebook. Symptom: HR's notebook and the employee's memory disagreeing; January's argument about December's days; the leaver's balance negotiated at exit. Disease: the number without the ledger (Ch. 5). Fix: the ledger grammar — allocations credit, applications debit, the balance always derived, the year sealed by ritual — and self-service showing the trail that ends the argument.

Pattern 4 — the never-taken leave. Symptom: balances compounding yearly; the indispensable person who never rests; the liability growing quietly. Disease: three at once (Ch. 1, 5, 7) — the wellbeing failure (burnout wearing dedication), the financial failure (the deferred cost the accountant will price), and the CONTROL failure the money tracks taught this academy to name: the person who never takes leave is one of fraud's classic tells, because schemes that need daily tending cannot survive their operator's absence — which is why mature control environments make leave MANDATORY for sensitive roles, and why the reconciler who hasn't rested in three years should worry a consultant more than the one who has. Fix: the use-it culture, the balance reads, and — for the custody and finance roles four tracks protected — the deliberate absence as a control, not a courtesy.

Pattern 5 — certification by suspicion. Symptom: sick-leave evidence demanded from some and waived for others; the rule flexing by standing. Disease: trust calibrated per person instead of per policy (Ch. 4). Fix: the threshold written, applied evenly, reviewed against pattern reads — the policy doing the trusting so no supervisor has to.

Pattern 6 — holiday chaos. Symptom: the declared holiday that surprises payroll; branches guessing whether they open; the Eid roster improvised at midnight. Disease: the list without its amendment flow (Ch. 6). Fix: the annual list ritual, the amendment protocol (update, re-roster, announce), and the holiday-working policy set before the year needs it.

The fourth law. The record, the pipeline, the capture — and now the entitlement: leave is an entitlement managed, not a favour negotiated — defined by policy on the statutory floor, granted as documents, spent through applications on the spine, kept as a ledger that always reconciles, planned against the trading year, and governed evenly at every edge from maternity to the last unspent day. The balance serves the employee's clarity, the manager's coverage, and the accountant's provision at once; the December that trades and the workforce that rests stop being rivals. Module 5 turns from the year's rhythm to the person's growth: performance — the conversation with a record.
