performance.title: HR 5 — Performance & Appraisals
performance.desc: Performance as a conversation with a record: goals and KRAs selected from the operational reads the firm already runs, the evidence layer that kills recency and halo, the appraisal cycle with calibration, ratings discipline with anchored scales, the continuous feedback layer, and underperformance met with process and support.

lessons.title: Chapter 1 — Performance: the conversation with a record
lessons.html:
The track's first four modules governed presence; this one governs contribution — and its thesis holds two ideas in one sentence: performance is a conversation with a record. Drop either half and the machinery fails in its own characteristic way.

The two failure modes. No performance management — the commoner disease in the trade: no goals, no reviews, no record; contribution assessed by impression, promotion by proximity (the person the owner sees most rises fastest — module 1's founder-bottleneck breeding its succession the same way), correction by explosion (nothing said for months, then everything at once), and the good quiet performer invisible until they resign. Performance theatre — the corporate import gone hollow: forms filled annually because the calendar says so, ratings assigned from a fortnight's memory, documents filed and never referenced, the whole exercise costing days and changing nothing — the appraisal as ritual without a reader, which is this academy's definition of waste (every ritual it has ever installed had a read and a consequence). The cure is the thesis's two halves working together: the CONVERSATION continuous (feedback near events, check-ins on a cadence — Chapter 6), and the RECORD periodic and evidence-based (the appraisal that references what the year actually shows — Chapters 3-5), each keeping the other honest: conversation without record evaporates; record without conversation ambushes.

The never-ambush law, promoted. Module 3 taught it for attendance; this module makes it the performance layer's constitution: nothing in an appraisal should be news. The rating that surprises, the weakness first named in the annual meeting, the goal the person learns they missed after the year ends — each is a failure of the continuous half, and each converts a development instrument into a grievance generator. The test the consultant teaches managers: before the appraisal meeting, ask has everything on this form already been said, closer to when it happened? — and if not, the form is not ready, the manager is.

What this module is for, honestly. The performance layer's products, named so the machinery stays aimed: DEVELOPMENT first (the person who knows where they stand and what growth looks like — module 6 consumes this module's outputs directly), DECISIONS second (the confirmation, the promotion, the increment recommendation, the improvement plan — each better made from records than impressions, with the money computations themselves living across the payroll boundary as always), and FAIRNESS throughout (the quiet performer made visible by evidence; the connected performer measured by the same scale — the pipeline's structured-interview argument, replayed annually for everyone already inside). What it is NOT for: surveillance theatre, rank-and-punish tournaments, or the imported bell curve applied to an eleven-person firm — the sizing honesty that has closed every thesis chapter closes this one: the machinery below fits a Nigerian trading firm's scale, and its heaviest instrument is a conversation.

lessons.title: Chapter 2 — Goals & KRAs: what good looks like, written down
lessons.html:
The performance conversation needs a subject, and the subject is set at the year's start: the GOALS — the written answer to what does good look like in this role, this year? The objective-setting chapter.

Goals from the role's actual work. The design source is the academy's own curriculum: the role's key result areas (KRAs) derive from what the role actually does and what the firm can actually observe — the till assistant's (session accuracy, the clean-close rate, service conduct), the storekeeper's (receiving discipline, count accuracy, the custody record), the collections officer's (the aging worked, the promises kept), the accountant's (the close's timeliness, the reconciliations' residue ages), the branch manager's (the branch scorecard's vitals — Inventory 6's page becoming a person's objectives). The insight that makes this trade's performance management CHEAPER than the corporate import: four tracks already built the measurements — the operational reads exist, are captured by machinery, and update without anyone filling a form — so the KRA layer largely SELECTS from evidence that already flows rather than inventing metrics that need feeding (Chapter 3's whole argument, previewed).

The goal disciplines. Probation's law (module 2), generalised to everyone: goals are FEW (three to five — the objective sheet with twelve goals prioritises nothing), OBSERVABLE (tied to evidence the year will actually produce — the goal nobody can measure becomes a mood at appraisal time), SHARED (the person holds the same sheet the manager holds, from the setting conversation — the appraisal against secret criteria is the trial with secret charges), and WEIGHTED where roles need it (the mix of operational KRAs and development goals — module 6's training path entering the sheet as a goal, which is how development stops being optional). Plus the honest balance the trade requires: goals include the QUALITATIVE where the role's value is qualitative (the service conduct, the team contribution — assessed by described behaviours, not invented numbers: a fake metric is worse than a frank judgment, because the judgment admits what it is).

Cascading, lightly. The firm's year shapes the sheets without drowning them: the firm-level goals (the year's few — the Akure ramp, the close's day-four target, the shrinkage band) cascade as CONTEXT and, where genuinely applicable, as shared objectives (the branch's team sharing the branch's vitals — the scorecard already published per module 6 of Inventory; the goal sheet simply points at it), and the cascade stops where relevance stops: the till assistant does not carry the firm's expansion goal; they carry the counter's excellence, which IS their contribution to it. The one-page rule closes the chapter: a person's year fits on a page — the goals, the weights, the evidence sources, the signatures of the setting conversation — and that page is the appraisal's skeleton, written in January so December can only confirm what the year already said.

lessons.title: Chapter 3 — The evidence layer: appraisals that reference records
lessons.html:
The chapter that makes this module the academy's own: the appraisal's evidence is largely ALREADY CAPTURED — by the machinery four tracks installed — and the performance layer's job is to organise it per person, not to invent it. The evidence chapter.

The inventory of existing evidence. What the systems already know, per role, without a single performance form: the TILL roles — session records (clean closes, variances, the streaks module 2's probation already used), service interactions where captured; the WAREHOUSE roles — receiving records (the count-before-sign discipline visible in every receipt's trail), cycle-count accuracy, custody counts signed, the adjustment history (the storekeeper whose locations count clean is holding a provable standard); the DRIVER roles — the tailgate reconciliations, the run records, the seal history; the SALES roles — the attributed revenue, the margin quality, the credit outcomes of their customers (the selling track's reads per person); the FINANCE roles — the close's lines owned and their timeliness, reconciliation residue ages, correction-log entries by author (Accounts 2's aggregate tells, read per person as craft evidence); and EVERYONE — the attendance layer (module 3's rates, as context: one stream, never the whole story), the training record (module 6's completions and scores — the academy's own certifications as performance evidence), and the conduct file (recognitions and documented conversations — Chapter 6).

The evidence folder, accumulated. The per-person organisation: through the year, the evidence ACCUMULATES against the goal sheet (the manager's log — Chapter 6 — plus the operational reads' periodic snapshots: the quarter's session summary attached, the count-accuracy read filed), so the appraisal is ASSEMBLED, not composed — the December meeting opens a folder that already tells the year's story, and the writing is synthesis, not archaeology. The economics the consultant sells: this is the audit-file argument (Accounts 7) applied to people — the system that runs well evidences well, and the firm already paying for operational discipline gets its performance evidence free.

Recency and halo, killed by records. The two memory diseases every un-evidenced appraisal carries, named so the cure is understood: RECENCY (the year rated by its last six weeks — the strong November erasing the weak spring, or the one December error erasing a strong year) and HALO (the general impression colouring every specific rating — the likeable person scored high on accuracy nobody checked). Both die the same death: the folder's evidence is dated and spans the year, so the rating conversation reads the YEAR — the quarterly snapshots outvoting the last fortnight's impression — and disagreements resolve by opening records instead of comparing recollections (the drill-before-disputing culture of Accounts 1, at the appraisal table).

The evidence boundary. The discipline that keeps the layer trusted: evidence is used WITH the person's knowledge (the goal sheet named its sources in January — nobody is surprised in December that their sessions were read, because the reading was the deal), CONTEXTUALISED (the variance rate of the till that handles triple the traffic is read against its volume; the count accuracy of the location with the hardest stock is read against its difficulty — evidence without context is a number pretending to be a judgment), and BALANCED (the operational reads measure what they measure; the qualitative half of the role gets its qualitative assessment — the machine's numbers inform the conversation and never replace it). The layer's one-sentence constitution: records make the appraisal honest; the manager makes it fair.

lessons.title: Chapter 4 — The appraisal cycle: the machinery
lessons.html:
The periodic record's machinery: the cycle defined, the document structured, the ratings calibrated, and the meeting run as a conversation. The cycle chapter.

The cycle. The working norm for the trade: the ANNUAL appraisal (the full record — goals reviewed, evidence assembled, ratings given, the development plan written) with the MID-YEAR check (the lighter formal touchpoint — on track or course-correcting, the goal sheet amended where the year changed it: the mid-probation review's logic, annualised for everyone), riding the continuous layer of Chapter 6 beneath both. The calendar discipline: the cycle's dates fixed and published (module 8's calendar), the season bounded (appraisals completed within the stated window — the season that drags to March is rating a year nobody remembers), and the sequence deliberate (self-assessment first, then the manager's, then the meeting — each stage feeding the next).

The appraisal document. The structure, section by section: the GOAL REVIEW (each goal from January's sheet: the evidence, the outcome, the rating — the skeleton filled), the SELF-ASSESSMENT (the person's own account first — because the self-assessment read before the manager writes theirs surfaces the perception gaps early, and the person who rates themselves honestly low on a real gap has started the development conversation themselves), the MANAGER'S ASSESSMENT (evidence-referenced, specific, written in the language of behaviours and results — the receiving discipline held on all forty-one receipts sampled beats good worker in every way that matters later), the OVERALL RATING (Chapter 5's discipline), and the DEVELOPMENT PLAN (the forward half — the growth areas, the training path additions, module 6's intake: an appraisal without a development plan is a verdict without a sentence, and development is the sentence this system wants).

Calibration: ratings consistent across managers. The multi-manager firm's quiet quality machinery, at trade scale: before ratings finalise, the managers' proposed ratings are REVIEWED TOGETHER (the calibration session — HR convening, the spine's managers present: each manager's distribution visible beside the others', the outliers discussed against evidence), because uncalibrated ratings measure the MANAGER (the lenient one whose team is uniformly outstanding; the harsh one whose identical team is uniformly average), and every downstream decision — increments, promotions, the improvement conversations — inherits the distortion. The session's rules: evidence talks (the challenged rating defends itself from the folder, not the podium), the goal is CONSISTENCY not a forced curve (the bell curve imposed on an eleven-person firm manufactures injustice to satisfy a template — the academy's sizing honesty, again: small teams can genuinely be mostly good, and the calibration confirms it rather than denying it), and the session's adjustments are made BEFORE meetings, so the person hears one message, once.

The meeting. The conversation the whole cycle exists to enable: scheduled properly (time protected, privacy real), structured as a dialogue (the self-assessment discussed, the evidence walked, the rating explained — not a form read aloud at a silent listener), forward-weighted (the development plan getting the meeting's second half — the past is the evidence; the future is the point), and closed with signatures and the shared record (the person's comments field theirs to use, including disagreement — the appraisal they can annotate is the appraisal they can trust). The never-ambush test applied one final time at the door: if any line of the form is news, the meeting is happening a year late.

lessons.title: Chapter 5 — Ratings discipline: the scale & its honesty
lessons.html:
The rating is the appraisal's most consequential compression — a year into a mark — and this chapter is the discipline that keeps the mark meaning something. The scale chapter.

The scale, anchored. The firm's scale (the common five points serve) defined with ANCHORS — each point a described standard, not a number with a vibe: what 'exceeds' looks like in evidence (the goals surpassed with the records to show it), what 'meets' means (the year delivered as the sheet defined — the anchor the consultant defends hardest, because 'meets' must be an honourable rating in a healthy system: the solid performer who did exactly what good looks like is the firm's backbone, and a culture where 'meets' reads as failure inflates every rating above it within two cycles), what the development points mean (the gap named, the plan attached), and what the lowest means (the improvement process engaged — Chapter 7). The anchors are published — everyone rates and is rated against the same descriptions — and the goal sheet's evidence sources make each anchor testable.

The rating diseases, named. The distortions every rating system breeds, taught so managers recognise their own: CENTRAL TENDENCY (everything a middle rating — the manager avoiding both the difficult conversation and the increment argument, producing a distribution that says nothing), LENIENCY (everything high — kindness in the moment, cruelty at the system level: the inflated team's genuine star is indistinguishable from its passengers, the underperformer ambushed years later by a file of 'outstanding' ratings that make the honest conversation legally awkward — the leniency that feels kind is the ambush's co-author), HALO and its inverse (Chapter 3's memory disease, at rating time), and the SPILL diseases (the attendance blemish bleeding into the craft rating; the personality friction rating the work — the scale rates the goal sheet, and the goal sheet named its subjects). The calibration session (Chapter 4) is where the diseases meet daylight: distributions compared, anchors re-read, evidence opened.

The distribution read. HR's post-season read, at altitude: the ratings' shape per team and per manager (the all-outstanding team is a leniency flag or a genuine unit — the evidence folder says which; the no-development-points team suggests avoidance; the year-on-year drift maps inflation), read as QUESTIONS for next season's calibration, never as quotas for this one — the read improves the raters, not the numbers.

Decoupled but connected: ratings and money. The boundary discipline that keeps both systems honest: the rating FEEDS decisions (the increment recommendation, the promotion case, the improvement process — each citing the appraisal), but the money computations live where money lives (the increment matrix, the bonus arithmetic — the payroll boundary and the owner's budget), and the appraisal meeting is NOT a salary negotiation (the meeting that becomes one stops being a development conversation permanently — the two conversations scheduled apart, deliberately, so the rating can be honest without being a bid). And the WRITTEN RATIONALE closes the chapter's discipline: every rating carries its paragraph — the evidence cited, the anchor referenced — because the rating that cannot explain itself in writing is an impression wearing a number, and every process this rating will ever feed (the promotion panel, the improvement plan, the dispute) will ask for the paragraph the lazy rating didn't write.

lessons.title: Chapter 6 — The continuous layer: feedback, recognition & the log
lessons.html:
The year between appraisals is where performance actually happens — and the continuous layer is the conversation half of the thesis, structured lightly enough to survive real management. The everyday chapter.

Feedback near events. The layer's first law: feedback lands CLOSE to what it concerns — the correction at week one (the receiving shortcut named the week it appeared: a two-minute conversation and a habit adjusted) versus the same correction at month twelve (an appraisal grievance and a habit calcified) — and the arithmetic the consultant teaches managers is the escalation-path economics of module 3, generalised: early feedback is cheap and effective; deferred feedback is expensive and resented, and the deferral is usually the manager's discomfort, not the person's unreadiness. The craft notes that make it land: specific (the behaviour, the instance, the impact — not the character), private for correction and public for recognition (the asymmetry that builds trust), and two-directional (the manager who asks what should I do differently? earns the right to be heard on everything else).

Recognition captured. The record's positive half — chronically under-built in firms that only document problems: the recognition RECORDED (the clean-audit quarter, the caught fraud attempt — Inventory's seal forensics finding its heroes, the customer's compliment, the colleague's cover during the maternity leave), lightly (a dated note to the file — the machinery is a text field, not a ceremony), and deliberately (the manager's monthly discipline: what went RIGHT this month, per person, noted) — because the evidence folder that holds only corrections misrepresents every year it summarises, and the appraisal drawn from it inherits the distortion. The culture dividend is larger than the record: the workforce that sees good work NOTICED — in writing, where it counts — supplies more of it; recognition is the cheapest performance intervention the firm owns.

The check-in cadence. The structured minimum between formal touchpoints: the manager's regular one-to-ones (monthly as the working norm for the trade — brief, scheduled, protected: the goal sheet glanced, the obstacles asked after, the notes kept), distinct from daily operational contact (the shift's traffic is not a check-in; the check-in is the fifteen minutes ABOUT the person, not the queue), and feeding the log. The sizing honesty: at eleven people this is the founder's few hours monthly, and it is precisely the founder-bottleneck's antidote in this layer — the check-ins that develop people are the delegation machinery being built, one conversation at a time.

The manager's log. The continuous layer's memory: the dated notes per person (feedback given, recognition recorded, check-in outcomes, the operational reads' notable moments) — kept in the system against the record (the custody rules of module 1 governing visibility — the log is the manager's and HR's, per the permission design), honest (notes written as if the person will read them, because processes exist in which they may — the discipline that keeps logs professional and defensible at once), and SUFFICIENT (the log is the appraisal's raw material: the December meeting that opens a year of dated notes writes itself; the one that opens a blank log writes fiction). The chapter's closing arithmetic, for the manager who calls this bureaucracy: five minutes a week of notes versus a December of archaeology and a grievance risk — the trade this academy has priced in every layer, at its most human scale.

lessons.title: Chapter 7 — Underperformance: the governed response
lessons.html:
The layer must also handle the hard case — the performance that persistently misses — and handle it as process, not improvisation. The chapter where fairness and firmness are the same discipline.

Capability versus conduct: the first distinction. The fork every case meets first, because the processes differ: CAPABILITY (the person trying and missing — skill, aptitude, or circumstance gaps: a performance-improvement matter, this chapter's terrain) versus CONDUCT (the person breaching rules — the lateness pattern refused, the policy violated, the integrity matter: the disciplinary machinery, module 7's terrain, with its own procedural requirements). The distinction matters legally and humanly — the capability case gets support and time; the conduct case gets the disciplinary procedure's protections — and the confused case (the capability gap prosecuted as misconduct, or the misconduct excused as a training need) fails both tests at once. The consultant's rule for managers: name which it is, in writing, before any process starts — and where genuinely mixed, run the processes as the distinct tracks they are.

The improvement frame. The capability response, structured (the PIP shape at consultant altitude — the adviser confirms the firm's procedural specifics): the GAP named in evidence (the goal sheet's specific shortfall, the records cited — not 'attitude', but the count accuracy at 91% against the 98% standard), the SUPPORT committed (the retraining, the mentor, the adjusted load — the plan that offers nothing is a dismissal letter with a waiting period, and tribunals read it as exactly that), the TIMELINE set (long enough to be real, bounded enough to be serious — the common eight-to-twelve-week shape), the REVIEWS held on their dates (the progress documented each time — the improvement plan that is never reviewed is theatre in both directions), and the OUTCOMES honest: improvement confirmed and the plan closed with its recognition (the person who climbed back deserves the note as much as the star — Chapter 6's positive record at its most meaningful), or the gap persisting and the process concluding as the employment framework provides (module 7's separation machinery, entered with a file that shows the firm tried — which is simultaneously the legal protection, the ethical position, and the culture signal to everyone watching, because everyone IS watching how the firm treats its strugglers).

The dignity discipline. The frame's conduct rules, because the process is a person's hardest season: confidentiality held (the improvement plan is not branch gossip — module 1's custody at its most pointed), the tone developmental (the meetings about the work, not the worth), the person heard (their account of the gap may contain the fix — the equipment, the rota, the training miss nobody made), and the manager supported too (the first PIP a manager runs needs HR beside them — the process failing on procedure helps no one, least of all the person it concerns).

The system read. The layer's aggregate honesty, closing the chapter: improvement cases read at altitude (the cluster under one manager is a management question; the cluster in one role is a design question — the role that everyone fails was mis-scoped or mis-hired, and module 2's pipeline wants that finding; the cluster after a change is the change's bill arriving) — because a firm's underperformance pattern is diagnostic BEFORE it is disciplinary, and the consultant who reads it that way fixes systems where others cycle through people. The chapter's law in one line: the response to persistent underperformance is a process with support, evidence, and an honest end — never a surprise, never a mood, never a corridor.

lessons.title: Chapter 8 — Case study: HealthTrade's first performance year
lessons.html:
The performance layer, run through its first full cycle. Every chapter clocks in.

The goal sheets (Ch. 2). January's setting conversations: one page per person, three to five goals each, evidence sources named. The till roles carry session accuracy and clean-close streaks; the storekeepers carry receiving discipline and count accuracy; the branch managers carry their scorecards' vitals plus one development goal each; the accountant carries the close's day-four target and residue ages. The firm's year (the Akure ramp, the shrinkage band) cascades as context — the branch teams pointing at scorecards already published, nobody carrying goals they cannot touch. The sheets signed, the sources understood: your sessions will be read — that is the deal, said in January, resented by no one in December.

The year between (Ch. 6). The monthly check-ins hold — imperfectly at first (two managers lapse in Q2; the HR nudge and the MD's modelling restore the cadence), then habitually. The logs accumulate: the recognition notes land (the Ibadan storekeeper's clean cycle-count quarter; the till assistant's handling of the disputed-price incident — the selling track's scenario, lived and noted), and the early corrections do their cheap work (a receiving shortcut named in week one at Akure — the two-minute conversation, the habit adjusted, the December that never hears of it because it ended in February).

The cycle runs (Ch. 3-4). The mid-year checks amend three goal sheets honestly (the year changed — the clinic line's launch redrew one role). December's season: self-assessments first (two perception gaps surface early and get their conversations before the meetings), evidence folders opened (the quarterly snapshots outvoting recency — one manager's draft, leaning on a strong November, revises against the spring's records), and the CALIBRATION session earns its chapter: the Lagos manager's distribution sits visibly above the others'; the anchors are re-read, three ratings defend themselves from folders and two revise — the leniency caught before it reached a single meeting, the manager coached, not scolded ('meets' is an honourable rating here — your solid people deserve a scale that says so).

The hard case and the promotion (Ch. 5, 7). One improvement case: a warehouse assistant's count accuracy persistently under standard — named in evidence (91% against 98%), supported (retraining plus a fortnight paired with the Ibadan storekeeper), timelined at ten weeks, reviewed on dates — and CLOSED with improvement confirmed at 97.5%, the recognition note filed (the climb-back documented as deliberately as the gap). And one promotion case built entirely from records: the Akure storekeeper — hired by module 2's practical (the candidate who caught the short), confirmed on evidence, a year of clean receiving and two caught discrepancies in the log — proposed for senior storekeeper with a file that argues itself: the panel reads for ten minutes and approves. The MD's season note joins the collection: we promoted from a folder, not a feeling — and everyone could see why. The layer's first year ends with ratings people trust, development plans feeding module 6's machinery, and the thesis demonstrated: the conversation happened all year; the record just proved it.

lessons.title: Chapter 9 — Common mistakes & the fifth law
lessons.html:
The performance layer's scar tissue. Symptom → disease → fix.

Pattern 1 — the annual ambush. Symptom: ratings that surprise; weaknesses first named in December; grievances filed the week after appraisal season. Disease: the record without the conversation (Ch. 1, 6) — the continuous half missing. Fix: feedback near events, the check-in cadence, the manager's log — and the door test enforced: if any line of the form is news, the meeting is a year late.

Pattern 2 — performance theatre. Symptom: forms completed, filed, never referenced; ratings from a fortnight's memory; the season costing days and changing nothing. Disease: ritual without a reader (Ch. 1) — the record without consequence. Fix: appraisals wired to their consumers (the development plans feeding module 6, the ratings feeding decisions with written rationales), the evidence folder replacing memory, and the cycle's outputs READ — or the cycle honestly retired, because theatre is worse than nothing: it teaches that records lie.

Pattern 3 — the everyone-outstanding team. Symptom: uniform top ratings; the genuine star invisible; the eventual honest conversation legally awkward against years of inflated files. Disease: leniency — kindness in the moment, cruelty at the system level (Ch. 5). Fix: anchored scales with 'meets' defended as honourable, the calibration session with evidence talking, the distribution read as questions — and the manager coached that inflation is the ambush's co-author.

Pattern 4 — the recency appraisal. Symptom: years rated by their final six weeks; strong springs erased by weak Novembers and vice versa. Disease: memory doing evidence's job (Ch. 3). Fix: the evidence folder with dated, year-spanning records; quarterly snapshots filed; disagreements resolved by opening records — the drill-before-disputing culture at the appraisal table.

Pattern 5 — capability confused with conduct. Symptom: the struggling worker prosecuted as a misconduct case, or the rule-breaker excused into endless retraining; processes that fail both tests. Disease: the fork never named (Ch. 7). Fix: the written designation before any process starts, the improvement frame for capability with real support, the disciplinary machinery for conduct with its protections — and mixed cases run as the distinct tracks they are.

Pattern 6 — promotion by proximity. Symptom: the person the owner sees most rising fastest; the branch's quiet excellence passed over; promotion announcements that surprise and demoralise. Disease: decisions from impressions in a layer built for evidence (Ch. 1, 8) — the founder-bottleneck breeding its succession. Fix: promotion cases built from folders (the goal sheets, the ratings with rationales, the logs), argued to a panel where scale permits, and the standard visible — the workforce that sees folders decide supplies its ambition to the folder, which is exactly the behaviour the firm wants.

The fifth law. The record, the pipeline, the capture, the entitlement — and now the contribution: performance is a conversation with a record — goals few, observable, and shared from January; evidence accumulated by the machinery the firm already runs; feedback near events and recognition in writing; ratings anchored, calibrated, and explained; underperformance met with process and support; and nothing in any appraisal ever news. The conversation develops the person; the record makes it fair, and each keeps the other honest. Module 6 takes the appraisal's forward half — the development plan — and builds the machinery that delivers it: training, by design.

training.title: HR 6 — Training & Development
training.desc: People developed by design: the skill map and needs register, curricula per role built from the firm's own truth, delivery through sessions and the trainer layer, certification with serials gating authority, measurement with before/after reads, and the development ladder with succession as the two-names law for capabilities.

lessons.title: Chapter 1 — Developed by design, not found
lessons.html:
Module 5 ended every appraisal with a development plan; this module builds the machinery that delivers them — and its thesis confronts the trade's favourite hiring myth head-on: people are developed by design, not found.

The hire-ready myth. The belief the consultant hears in every engagement: we just need to find good people — as if the market stocks ready-made storekeepers who count before signing, till operators who close clean, and accountants who run day-four closes, and the firm's only job is shopping well. The market rarely sells ready-made — it sells RAW MATERIAL of varying quality (module 2's pipeline selects the best of it: aptitude, integrity, the instincts the practical test surfaces), and everything after selection is MANUFACTURE: the disciplines this academy spent four tracks defining are learned behaviours, taught deliberately or absorbed accidentally, and the firm that relies on absorption gets exactly the inconsistency it observes — the branch whose standards live in whoever trained whom, informally, years ago. The reframe for owners: hiring buys potential; training converts it — and the conversion is the firm's job, because nobody else will do it to the firm's standard.

Training as infrastructure, not event. The second reframe: training in the unstructured firm is an EVENT (the workshop someone attended once, the induction that happened to early staff and faded, the vendor session at go-live) — and events decay, because people join after them, forget past them, and drift beyond them. Training as INFRASTRUCTURE is the standing machinery: curricula that exist per role (Chapter 3), delivered on demand to every joiner and every promotion (the onboarding path of module 2; the development plans of module 5), assessed so completion means competence (Chapter 5's whole argument), refreshed as the firm's practices evolve, and READ like every other layer (Chapter 6's measurement). The economics repeat the academy's oldest trade: the curriculum built once teaches forever — the storm of every-hire-improvised-induction becomes the weather of a path assigned in an afternoon.

The meta note, made explicit. This module has an unusual property the consultant should notice and use: the machinery it describes is the machinery DELIVERING it — a role-based curriculum, structured modules, proctored assessment, certification with serials — because the academy this certification belongs to IS the pattern at work: the consultant reading this chapter inside a training path, tracked by completion, gated by a proctored bank, is holding the proof that the pattern scales from a software vendor's consultant corps to a three-branch pharmacy's till roster. The pitch to clients writes itself: the system that trained me can train your people — same machinery, your content — and Chapter 3 will show exactly how the pattern transfers.

The scope line. What this module covers: needs, curricula, delivery, certification, measurement, and paths — the people-development machinery. What stays at its boundaries: the statutory training obligations of regulated roles (the superintendent pharmacist's continuing-education requirements — tracked here, defined by the regulator and the professional), and the formal-education sponsorships with their bonds (module 4's study-leave machinery holding that edge). The module's map follows capability's life: found (needs), built (curricula and delivery), proven (certification), verified (measurement), and grown (paths) — the manufacture, end to end.

lessons.title: Chapter 2 — The training needs picture
lessons.html:
Design starts from needs, and the needs are not guessed — they are READ, from sources the firm already runs. The detection chapter.

The skill map: the reference grid. The foundation artifact: per ROLE (module 1's designation list earning another dividend), the required competences listed — the till role's (the sale, the return, the cash-up, the disputed-price handling, the till policies), the storekeeper's (receiving discipline, counting, the custody documents, the location system), the accountant's (the close's lines, the reconciliations, the correction doctrine) — at the levels the role needs (aware / competent / able-to-teach: three levels serve the trade; five serve consultancies). The map is the layer everything else references: the GAP analysis (each person against their role's row — the visual that turns 'training needs' from a mood into a list), the onboarding path's syllabus (the role's row IS the curriculum outline — Chapter 3), and the succession read (Chapter 7's single-point capabilities are the map's columns with one name in them). Built once with the managers (a half-day per role family), maintained as roles evolve — the map is a master, governed like one.

The intake channels. Where needs arrive from, each channel already flowing: appraisal development plans (module 5's forward half — the plans aggregated per season become the training demand book: twelve people needing the costing module is a scheduled cohort, not twelve promises), the operational reads as needs detectors (the academy's quiet gift to this module: the error CLUSTERS are needs wearing incident clothes — the receiving discipline slipping at one branch is a refresher flag before it is a disciplinary question; the correction-log entries clustering on one journal type is a finance-training finding; module 5's improvement cases arriving with their gaps pre-named), onboarding (every hire and promotion triggering the role's path — module 2's checklist line, feeding this machinery), compliance and regulation (the regulated trade's mandated competences — the pharmacy's requirements, the fire-and-safety layer, the certifications with expiry dates Chapter 5 tracks), and the firm's own changes (the new product line, the new module going live, the policy that changed — every change this academy's other tracks taught the firm to make as an event carries a training line in its rollout, which is why the corridor-toggle conviction kept insisting changes be announced: the announcement IS micro-training).

The needs register. The channels converge on one governed list: the training needs register — each need with its source (the appraisal, the read, the regulation), its population (who needs it), its priority (the compliance need outranks the aspiration; the bleeding read outranks both), and its disposition (the path assigned, the event scheduled, the cohort formed — or the honest deferral with a date). Read quarterly (module 8's calendar), the register converts development from a sentiment into a pipeline — and its aggregate tells its own story: the register dominated by remedial needs is a firm whose entries leak (module 2's early-attrition logic applied to competence); the one dominated by growth needs is a firm whose foundation holds. The consultant reads the register's SHAPE before its lines — the diagnosis-before-prescription habit, at the capability layer.

lessons.title: Chapter 3 — The curriculum per role: training paths
lessons.html:
The needs become teachable through CURRICULA — the role-based paths that turn the skill map's rows into structured, assessable journeys. The design chapter, and the pattern this academy itself proves.

The path's anatomy. Per role (or role family), the training path: MODULES in sequence (each covering one competence area — the till path's product module, sales module, till-operations module, policies module; the storekeeper's receiving, counting, custody, and systems modules), each module holding LESSONS (the readable units — text, images, the short video where it earns its place: the mock delivery filmed once teaches forever) and its ASSESSMENT (Chapter 5's machinery — the quiz that gates completion), the path ordered by dependency (the product knowledge before the sale; the document flow before the exception handling), and sized honestly (the till path a new hire completes inside probation; the consultant path a quarter's journey — the path that cannot be completed alongside the job is a path that won't be).

Content from the firm's own truth. The design law that separates working curricula from shelfware: the content teaches THE FIRM'S actual practice — its documents, its policies, its screens, its scenarios (the disputed-price lesson uses the firm's price-dispute policy; the receiving lesson walks the firm's actual receiving flow with its actual forms) — because generic content teaches generic behaviour, and the gap between the course and the counter is where training dies. The sourcing economics: the firm's practices are ALREADY WRITTEN (four tracks of policy pages, checklists, and process documents — the academy's documentation-as-byproduct thesis paying its development dividend: the curriculum is the policy page, taught), and the maintenance discipline follows (the policy that changes updates its lesson — the curriculum versioned with the practices it teaches, or it quietly becomes a museum of the old way).

Assessment as the gate. The path's spine: each module ASSESSED (the question bank per module, the pass mark, the proctored mode where stakes warrant — timed, served from a bank large enough that retakes meet fresh questions), completion meaning DEMONSTRATED (Chapter 5 will hammer this: attendance is not learning; the certificate that only proves presence gates nothing safely), and retakes governed (allowed — the goal is competence, not filtration — with the retake pattern read: the module everyone fails twice is a content problem or a bank problem, and the read fixes the course before it blames the class).

Assignment and progress. The path's lifecycle in the machinery: ASSIGNED at the trigger (onboarding's checklist line; the appraisal's development plan; the promotion's new-role requirements — module 7's transfer machinery will add its own trigger), tracked visibly (the person sees their path and progress in self-service — the same transparency dividend as every layer; the manager sees the team's — the path stalled at module two for a month is a check-in topic, not a mystery), and COMPLETED into the record (the completions and scores landing in module 5's evidence folder and Chapter 5's certification register — training results as performance evidence, the loop this track keeps closing). The meta note made operational: this paragraph describes the exact machinery serving this exact lesson — assignment, progress, proctored gates, records — and the consultant configuring it for a client is installing the pattern they are currently inside.

lessons.title: Chapter 4 — Programs & events: the delivery machinery
lessons.html:
Paths carry the standing curriculum; PROGRAMS and EVENTS carry the live layer — the sessions, drills, and cohorts where people learn together. The delivery chapter.

The internal session: the trade's workhorse. The firm teaching itself, structured: the branch practical (the mock delivery run at the actual gate — Inventory's receiving discipline drilled with a staged carton and a deliberately short document; the till drill on the training instance — the disputed price, the shortpay, the cash-up rehearsed where mistakes are free), the classroom hour (the policy walkthrough, the new-module introduction), and the toolbox session (the fifteen-minute shift-start refresher — the lightest unit, and for the trade often the highest-yield: one scenario, one reminder, done before the doors open). The design disciplines: sessions have OBJECTIVES (what the attendee can DO after that they couldn't before — the session without one is a meeting wearing a flipchart), MATERIALS kept (the session pack filed — taught once, reusable), and the practical bias the trade demands (the ratio tilted toward doing: the receiving lesson that is 80% watching is 20% learning).

The trainer layer: teaching as development. The delivery force is the firm's own seniors — and the design insight with the double dividend: the senior storekeeper teaching receiving is simultaneously delivering training AND being developed (the able-to-teach level of Chapter 2's map is a competence in its own right — the teacher must articulate what they do by instinct, which deepens the instinct; and the teaching role is the pre-supervisory test module 7's ladder will read). The governance: trainers are NAMED per module (the map's able-to-teach column populated deliberately), prepared (the trainer's session pack, the first delivery observed), and recognised (the teaching noted in module 5's recognition layer — the firm that treats teaching as extra work unpaid teaches its seniors to hoard knowledge, which is the single-point disease being actively cultivated).

The training event as a record. Every delivery documented — the event record: what was taught (the module, the version), by whom, to whom (the attendance captured — module 3's discipline reaching the classroom), with what assessment outcome (the post-session check where the content warrants one), and filed. The record's consumers make the case for the discipline: the compliance audit (the regulated trade asked WHO was trained on the safety procedure, WHEN — the register answers or the firm improvises), the incident review (the error's actor trained or not trained is the first fork in every root-cause tree — trained-and-erred is coaching; never-trained-and-erred is the FIRM'S error wearing the person's name), and the measurement layer (Chapter 6 needs the before/after line, and the event record is the 'after' begins here marker).

External programs. The bought layer, governed: the external course selected against the needs register (not the brochure's charisma), the attendee BRIEFED with the reuse expectation (the returning attendee teaches the toolbox session — the bought knowledge multiplied instead of filed), the certificate landing in Chapter 5's register with its expiry where it carries one, and the spend read annually against Chapter 6's evidence (the external budget that produces no behaviour change buys travel, not training). The sizing honesty as always: the eleven-person firm's delivery machinery is a senior, a checklist, and a staged carton — the SHAPE, at teaspoon scale, and fully sufficient.

lessons.title: Chapter 5 — Certification & competence: records that gate authority
lessons.html:
The layer that converts training from activity into ASSURANCE: certification — the proven-competence record — and its highest use: gating authority. The chapter where this track meets every other track's permission designs.

Internal certification: completion means demonstrated. The proctored assessment as the gate (the timed quiz served from the bank, the pass mark set to mean something, the certificate issued with its SERIAL — the register's law, at the competence layer: numbered, dated, revocable, never reissued casually), and the conviction the chapter hammers: attendance is not learning — the sign-in sheet proves presence; the assessment proves competence; and everything this chapter gates (the authorities below) must gate on the assessment, because gating on attendance is gating on nothing wearing a lanyard. The certification's scope is stated on its face (certified for WHAT — the module, the version, the role level), and re-certification exists where practices drift or stakes demand currency (the annual re-take for the safety layer; the version-triggered refresh when the policy that was taught changed).

External certifications: tracked with expiries. The bought and regulated layer in the same register: the professional licences (the pharmacist's — the regulated trade's trading licence wearing a person's name), the statutory certificates (fire safety, first aid, the forklift), and the vendor certifications — each recorded against the person with its EXPIRY, feeding module 1's expiry worklist (the machinery already built: surfaced 60 and 30 days out, owned, worked), because the expired licence discovered by the inspector is the compliance failure that was a calendar entry all along. The regulated-role read: the roles that legally REQUIRE current certification listed, the register's coverage checked monthly (the branch whose superintendent's licence lapses cannot lawfully trade its regulated lines — the certification register is trading infrastructure, exactly as the branch door's device was).

Competence gating authority: the chapter's summit. The design pattern that makes this module load-bearing for the whole academy: the AUTHORITIES four tracks assigned — the closing-authorised roster (module 3's till count and cash-up), the adjust permission's two names (Inventory 8), the journal pen (Accounts 2), the receiving sign-off, the price-override right — each maps to a COMPETENCE, and the mature firm wires the mapping: authority follows certification — the closing roster admits the till-certified; the adjustment names hold the counting certification; the new branch's authority matrix (Inventory 6's playbook) is staffed from the certified register, not from availability. The dividend runs both directions: the authority granted on proven competence is defensible (the incident review that finds a certified actor asks different questions than one that finds an improvised grant), and the certification WANTED because it unlocks (the development path acquires teeth — the ambitious till assistant knows exactly what stands between them and the closing roster, and it is a curriculum, not a relationship: the anti-favouritism machinery of this whole track, expressed as a syllabus).

The certified register. The layer's standing artifact: who holds what, current, per branch and role — the coverage view (every authority's certified population per branch: the single-certified capability is Chapter 7's succession flag raised automatically), the expiry horizon (the quarter's renewals visible), and the audit face (the register that answers the compliance question, the incident question, and the staffing question from one page). Governed as a master, read monthly, and joined everywhere — the fifth master's competence shadow, and the page module 8's analytics will summarise.

lessons.title: Chapter 6 — Measuring training: did it work?
lessons.html:
The layer's honesty chapter: training consumes hours and money, and the firm deserves to know whether it changed anything. Measurement at working altitude — the levels, the reads, and the redesign discipline.

The levels, at trade altitude. The classic evaluation ladder, sized for a trading firm: reaction (did attendees rate it useful — the lightest signal, collected in a minute, predictive of little but worth having: the session everyone rated confusing needs its content read before its results), learning (the assessment scores — Chapter 5's gates producing this level automatically: pass rates, score distributions, the retake patterns), behaviour (the level that matters most and costs least in THIS firm — because the operational reads ARE behaviour measurement: the receiving discipline's error rate, the session variance rate, the count accuracy, the correction-log clusters — all captured continuously by machinery four tracks installed, so the question did the training change behaviour? is answered by reads the firm already runs), and results (the business numbers the behaviour serves — the shrinkage band, the close's day count, the collection rate: moved by many causes, read with that honesty, but read).

The before/after discipline. The measurement pattern the consultant installs: the training intervention BOOKENDED — the baseline read taken before (the branch's receiving error rate for the quarter preceding), the intervention delivered and dated (Chapter 4's event record supplying the marker), the after read taken at the stated horizon (the following quarter's rate), and the movement attributed with appropriate modesty (the confound named where it exists — the same quarter's staff change, the season's volume shift; the honest sentence is the rate moved from X to Y across the intervention; here is what else moved — the epistemics of Accounts 6's variance decomposition, applied to people). The pattern's cheapness is its argument: both reads already exist; the discipline is only the bookending — dated, filed, compared.

Training ROI in the trade's own numbers. The owner conversation, equipped: the counting refresher priced (the trainer's afternoon, the attendees' hours) against the variance trend it moved (the shrinkage naira, the recount hours saved); the till drill against the session-variance decline; the pipeline's practical-test training against the early-attrition rate — the returns denominated in the same naira the reads already count, which is what makes the case land where 'training is important' never does. The honest boundary stated with it: not everything measurable matters and not everything that matters is measurable (the service culture, the confidence of the confirmed) — the numbers carry the argument they can carry, and the qualitative half gets its qualitative account, exactly as module 5's goal sheets ruled.

When training didn't work: redesign, not repeat. The failure discipline: the intervention whose after-read didn't move gets DIAGNOSED, not rescheduled — the fork tree: wrong diagnosis (the error cluster wasn't a knowledge gap — the equipment, the rota, the incentive: the training that teaches what people already know treats a system problem with a syllabus), wrong content (the generic course that never touched the firm's actual flow — Chapter 3's design law violated), wrong delivery (the watching-heavy session for a doing-heavy skill), or wrong gate (the pass mark that certified the incompetent — Chapter 5's bank and mark reviewed). The conviction closing the chapter: repeating failed training is the corridor toggle of the capability layer — the same intervention, expecting different behaviour, consuming goodwill each round — and the read-diagnose-redesign loop is what separates a training FUNCTION from a training calendar.

lessons.title: Chapter 7 — The development path & succession
lessons.html:
The module's forward horizon: capability built not just for today's role but for the next one — the ladder, the deputy, and the succession discipline that applies the two-names law to capabilities. The growth chapter.

The ladder per role family. The visible progression: the till family (assistant → senior till → counter supervisor), the warehouse family (storekeeper → senior storekeeper → ops lead), the finance family (Accounts 8's bookkeeper → accountant → controller, now with its training spine), the branch family (the supervisor → branch manager path the multi-branch firm must manufacture — Inventory 6's day-one-capable branch manager does not exist in the market at the firm's standard; the firm builds them or borrows them badly). Each rung DEFINED (the skill map's rows at the next level — what the senior storekeeper must hold that the storekeeper needn't; the certifications the rung requires — Chapter 5's gating giving the ladder its teeth), and the definition PUBLISHED: the ladder everyone can see converts ambition into curriculum (module 5's promotion-from-folders culture, given its syllabus — the anti-proximity machinery completed).

Development plans feeding ladders. The connection wired: module 5's development plans reference the ladder (the plan that says 'grow toward senior storekeeper' decomposes into the rung's named gaps — the modules to pass, the teaching to deliver, the exposure to gain), the path assigned accordingly (Chapter 3's machinery), and progress read at the check-ins (module 5's cadence carrying the development conversation, not just the performance one). The pace honesty: ladders are climbed in years, not quarters — the plan promising a rung annually to everyone is writing cheques the org structure cannot cash, and the honest ladder conversation includes the arithmetic (rungs open when the structure grows or seniors move — module 1's vanity-structure conviction guarding this exact door: the title manufactured to reward is the grade structure being spent like petty cash).

Succession: the two-names law for capabilities. The chapter's summit, and the roster's single-point discipline (module 3) applied to the capability layer: every CRITICAL capability — the certified register's columns that keep branches trading and books closing (the closing authority, the receiving sign-off, the close's owner, the superintendent's license-bearing role) — carries the question who is the second name? — and the succession read (quarterly, off the certified register: the capabilities with one current holder listed automatically) drives deliberate deputy development: the second person trained BEFORE the vacancy (the deputy who learned during the maternity cover — module 4's cover plan doubling as succession machinery; the senior developed against the ladder before the ops-lead need opens), because the alternative is the trade's familiar scramble — the resignation that orphans an authority, the promotion delayed by its own vacuum, the branch that cannot trade a Thursday. The framing for owners, in the academy's oldest voice: succession is not disloyalty planning; it is the handover test (every track's module 8) applied to people — the firm whose capabilities survive their holders has solved at the human layer what the documentation solved at the process layer.

Mentoring, formalised lightly. The pattern module 1's spine already carried (the Ibadan manager mentoring Akure): named pairs (the mentor chosen for the able-to-teach level and the temperament), a cadence (monthly, protected), a scope (the rung being climbed — the mentor walks their own old path), and the recognition loop (mentoring recorded as the senior contribution it is — module 5's log; Chapter 4's trainer dividend, extended). The chapter's closing line joins the thesis to the firm's future: the ladder is the curriculum's shadow, the deputy is the succession's answer, and both exist because the firm decided to manufacture its next generation instead of hoping to find it.

lessons.title: Chapter 8 — Case study: HealthTrade's development year
lessons.html:
The capability machinery, installed and run. Every chapter clocks in.

The map and the register (Ch. 2). The skill map built in three half-days with the managers: five role families, competences at three levels, the able-to-teach column populated honestly (thin — two names covering most of it: the single-point finding arriving before the succession chapter needed it). The needs register convenes its channels: the appraisal season's development plans (module 5's intake — eleven plans aggregating into four cohort needs), one operational-read flag (the correction log clustering on expense journals — a finance refresher scheduled), and the compliance layer confirmed (the superintendent's licence current, two fire-safety certificates expiring in Q3 — into the worklist).

The curricula deployed (Ch. 3). The till and storekeeper paths built from the firm's own pages — the policy documents, receiving checklists, and till procedures of four tracks becoming lessons in a fortnight (the documentation-as-byproduct dividend, cashed), each module gated by a proctored bank, sized to complete inside probation. Assigned to the two Akure hires mid-probation (their confirmation objectives already referencing the modules — module 2's machinery meshing), and to two existing staff whose gap analysis showed holes the informal era left. The retake read catches one content fault: the counting module's question everyone misses twice — a badly-anchored question, fixed in the bank, not blamed on the class.

The delivery layer (Ch. 4). The trainer roles named: the Ibadan storekeeper (the clean-cycle-count quarter of module 5's recognition) prepared and observed teaching the receiving practical — the staged carton, the deliberately short document — and the toolbox pattern lands at the branches: fifteen minutes, one scenario, before the Saturday doors. The event records file. The teaching dividend shows inside a quarter: the trainer's own receiving notes sharpen (articulating the instinct deepened it — the debrief line), and his log gains the senior-contribution entries the ladder will read.

Certification gates authority (Ch. 5). The certified register stands up, and the wiring completes: the closing-authorised roster (HR 3's Akure fix) now admits by till certification — the ambitious Akure till assistant (module 2's quiet candidate) sees the syllabus between her and the closing roster, completes it in six weeks, certifies, and joins the roster: a curriculum, not a relationship — the sentence the branch remembers. The adjustment names re-verified against counting certifications; the register's coverage view flags the single-certified capabilities for Chapter 7's read.

Measurement and succession (Ch. 6-7). The receiving refresher bookended: Akure's receiving error rate read for the prior quarter, the intervention dated, the after-read two quarters on — the rate halves, the confound named honestly (the same period's second hire), the ROI sentence filed in the trade's naira. And the succession read runs off the register: three single-name capabilities listed automatically — the close's owner, the receiving sign-off at Lagos, the ops-lead capability that doesn't exist yet — and the year's deliberate answer: the Ibadan storekeeper's development plan formalises toward ops lead (the ladder's rung defined, the mentor named — the MD himself, monthly, protected), the Lagos deputy trained before any vacancy asks, and the maternity cover of module 4 retro-recognised as the succession machinery it accidentally was. The MD's year-note: we used to hope the market would sell us our next ops lead; we are building him instead — and he taught the class that proved he could.

lessons.title: Chapter 9 — Common mistakes & the sixth law
lessons.html:
The capability layer's scar tissue. Symptom → disease → fix.

Pattern 1 — training as event. Symptom: the workshop attended once; the induction that faded after the founding staff; go-live training decaying with every hire since. Disease: events where infrastructure belongs (Ch. 1) — training that people join after, forget past, drift beyond. Fix: the standing curricula per role, assigned at every entry and promotion, versioned with the practices — the path, not the workshop.

Pattern 2 — the hire-ready myth. Symptom: 'we just need good people'; every gap answered by recruitment; the standards living in whoever trained whom informally. Disease: shopping where manufacture belongs (Ch. 1). Fix: the reframe (hiring buys potential; training converts it), the pipeline selecting raw quality, the curriculum doing the conversion — and the branch-consistency read as the proof the owner watches.

Pattern 3 — certificates without competence. Symptom: sign-in sheets as training records; authorities granted on attendance; the incident actor 'trained' by a register that only proves presence. Disease: attendance mistaken for learning (Ch. 5). Fix: assessment as the gate, proctored where stakes warrant, authority following certification — and the register's face stating what was PROVEN, not what was attended.

Pattern 4 — the untracked expiry. Symptom: the licence discovered lapsed by the inspector; the branch trading regulated lines on an expired superintendent; the first-aider whose certificate died quietly. Disease: compliance as memory (Ch. 5) — the calendar entry that was never entered. Fix: every dated certificate in the register feeding the expiry worklist, the regulated-coverage read monthly, renewals owned — the certification register treated as the trading infrastructure it is.

Pattern 5 — the single-point capability. Symptom: the one closer, the one signer, the one licence-holder; the resignation that orphans an authority; the Thursday the branch couldn't trade. Disease: the two-names law never applied to capabilities (Ch. 7). Fix: the succession read off the certified register (single-name columns flagged automatically), the deputy developed before the vacancy, cover plans read as succession machinery — capabilities that survive their holders.

Pattern 6 — development promised, never delivered. Symptom: appraisal plans that reference training which never happens; the same growth goals copied year to year; a workforce that learns the development plan is a pleasantry. Disease: the intake without the pipeline (Ch. 2) — module 5's forward half orphaned. Fix: the needs register with dispositions and dates, the plans aggregated into scheduled cohorts, the quarterly register read — and the credibility arithmetic taught to owners: one delivered plan buys more engagement than ten promised ones.

The sixth law. The record, the pipeline, the capture, the entitlement, the conversation — and now the manufacture: people are developed by design — needs read from the machinery the firm already runs, curricula built per role from the firm's own truth, delivery that biases toward doing, completion meaning demonstrated, authority following certification, results measured before and after, and every critical capability carrying a second name before the vacancy asks. The ladder converts ambition into curriculum; the register gates authority on proof; and the firm that manufactures its people stops shopping for what the market doesn't sell. Module 7 takes the lifecycle to its events and its end: promotions, transfers, discipline, and the clean separation.
